Pillars and Forces

Each Pillar is a felt reading a member holds about the group or her place in it, rated 1 to 10. Each force card says how one Pillar's level moves another's in the same member.

Reading the matrix

One row per force card. A filled dot marks the source Pillar and a ring marks the target, coloured by type. Select a row to open the card.

Reviews

Ratings and comments from Ben and invited reviewers on every Pillar and card. Open any Pillar or card to add your own. Ratings run from 1 (does not hold up) to 5 (holds up well).

CoPILAR, in development (provisional)

Full text of the model

Every Pillar and force card as plain text, generated from the model files. Use this page, or the files model.json and model.md, to point an AI or a reader at a specific part. Each heading has a stable anchor.

Claim ceiling. Synthetic reviews and simulated games show plausibility only. They generate hypotheses for human testing; they do not test ComPILAR.

Pillars

Team Confidence (GrpProsp)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How far you feel the group, as it now stands, can pull off the venture it has taken on and not yet finished: a game, project, season or campaign. It is confidence in the capability the venture will run on, not luck, not your own prospects (Payoff), not whether each will do their part (Dependability) and not a general sense that the group is strong. The culture's face sets where that capability is looked for.

10: You feel sure the group, as it stands, can pull off what it has set itself; the venture looks well within its reach.

1: You feel sure the group, as it stands, cannot pull off what it has set itself; the venture looks beyond it.

Pre-language: A felt sense, before any words, that this band can bring off what it is setting out to do: chimpanzee males who hear strangers chorus and advance together when their party holds three or more males, and stay silent or hold back when it holds fewer (Wilson et al. 2001); and the chimpanzee who picks as partner the one who has made a joint task work before (Melis et al. 2006). Intimates read it from her bearing as the venture starts: settled and forward-leaning, in step with the others, or hesitant and watchful, eyes on the others rather than the task.

Effect on Engagement: That is likely to succeed in goals that you believe are worth pursing, or you would not have joined the group in the first place, and that has agreed goals, or otherwise random changes to the group's direction will move outside the model's ability to predict.

Capability spread across the members. How far you feel the group, as it now stands, can pull off the venture it has agreed to take on and not yet finished. It is confidence in the group's capability for that venture, spread across its members, their skill included, and including whoever the band looks to for this venture for the day, so long as they lead by being followed and not by command. It is not luck, not your own prospects (Payoff), not whether each will do their part (Dependability), and not a general sense that the group is strong. 10: You feel sure the group, as it stands, can pull off what it has set itself; the venture looks well within its reach. 1: You feel sure the group, as it stands, cannot pull off what it has set itself; the venture looks beyond it.

Confidence in those who steer. How far you feel those at the top of the order, yourself included if you are there, can steer the group through the venture it has taken on and not yet finished: read the ground, choose the course, set each member to the part that suits them and right the course when it goes wrong. It reads their competence to direct this venture only. It is not whether they push you about or take more than their due (Parity), not the deference you draw for what you bring (Esteem), not your rung in the order (Rank), not what staying will bring you (Payoff), and not whether those below will carry their parts (Dependability). A well-meaning leader out of their depth rates low; a hard one who knows the way rates high. 10: You feel sure those at the top know the way through what the group has taken on; you follow their lead without second-guessing it, and if you are among them you feel the course is in safe hands. 1: You feel sure those at the top cannot steer the group through what it has taken on; each call they make looks like the wrong one, and if you are among them you feel the course slipping out of your hands.

Payoff (OwnProsp)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How likely you feel it is that staying in this group will get you what you yourself are after from it: the place, play, pay, skill, advancement or mate you joined for. It is a forecast of what the group will deliver to you, not your own ability, not your present rung in the order (Rank), not the group's own venture (Team Confidence), not whether help you give comes back (Reciprocity), and not a tally of what it has given so far, which only feeds it.

10: You are sure that staying will bring you what you came for; the group's dealings with you keep opening the way to it.

1: You are sure that staying will bring you nothing you came for; whatever you do here, the way to it stays shut.

Pre-language: The felt yield of staying with this band for her: whether being here keeps bringing her food, a mate, a place or a skill, or keeps bringing her nothing. Intimates read it from whether she settles in and works at her own aims here, or drifts to the edge, looks outward and leaves.

Effect on Engagement: Where you feel that you are likely to achieve your personal goals, whether or not they are part of the group goals (Team Confidence) or indeed, conflict with them. Presumably if personal and group goals are in conflict, you would prefer to have low levels of Team Confidence however such a condition is out of scope for the model as it indicates deception and potentially sabotage, which is a cognitive rather than an unconscious drive (as the Pillars are contended to be).

Rank (Status)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

Your felt rung in the group's settled order of precedence: how far you go first, take the first turn and the first share as a matter of course, and how far you go after others and take what is left. All recognise the order, so it is not fought out each time. The precedence attaches to your place, however you came by it: an office, seniority, the backing of kin or allies, an old contest no one reopens, or credit for what you bring that has settled, over time, into a place others take for granted. It is distinct from the live deference you draw for what you bring now (Esteem), and once settled it does not need present fear to hold it day to day (Parity), though an old contest or the backing of allies may stand behind it.

10: You go first as a matter of course: the first turn, the first share and the best seat are yours without a word said, and no one in the group stands above you.

1: You go last as a matter of course: you wait your turn and take your share and seat after everyone else, without a word said, and no one in the group stands below you.

Pre-language: Her felt rung in an order all recognise: the others let her pass, eat and settle first and greet her with the calm signals of submission, or she passes, eats and settles after them and greets them so, and neither side has to fight it out each time. Intimates read it from who passes first when paths cross, who eats first, who takes the best spot, and who greets whom.

Effect on Engagement: Where you feel that you possess formal power within a group, enabling you to utilise the group to achieve your own vision, which aligns the group with your identity. This is why new leaders often revoke measures taken by the preceding.

Rule-Keeping (NormExp)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How strongly it strikes you as wrong when another member breaks from the group's settled ways in a way the group would condemn, in act or by openly pressing to change them. It is felt indignation at a breach, not dislike of the person. Intimates read it from whether you pull the member up: an objection, mockery, a cold shoulder or shutting them out. Your own conformity and your openness to ideas are not part of it.

10: The smallest departure the group would condemn jars you at once as plainly wrong, and intimates see you pull the member up on the spot: a sharp word, a mocking laugh or a turned back.

1: A member breaking the group's settled ways, or openly pressing to change them, leaves you unmoved even where the group would condemn it; nothing in you says it is wrong, and intimates see you let it pass.

Pre-language: The bristle at one of the band doing a thing the wrong way. Its sign is the move to pull them up: a protest cry, a shove, a cold shoulder or exclusion. In one theft experiment, captive chimpanzees retaliated for their own losses but did not punish theft from others (Riedl et al. 2012). Intimates read it from how she meets another's departure: with indignation and a rebuke, or with a shrug. Forager bands such as the Ju/'hoansi turn a like bristle, by criticism and mockery, on upstarts and stingy members (Wiessner 2005); in this model that egalitarian form is carried by Safety->Parity and stands here only as the contrast. The face here is the guarding of a ranked group's settled ways.

Effect on Engagement: Where you feel that you can manage (minimise unwelcome or surprising) change, by using your power to reduce any propensity for others to suggest change. While high Rule-Keeping undermines Psychological Safety for others, it makes you personally feel safer.

Dependability (OutResp)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How far you feel the other members can be counted on to do their part in the shared work: each carries through what they take on and keeps their word about it, so you leave work in their hands without checking that they are doing it. It is reliability, not skill (Team Confidence): a member of modest skill who always carries through what they take on rates high. It reads their part, not the return on your help (Reciprocity), whether anyone takes more than their due of shares, credit or say and makes it stick (Parity), or their verdict on your own conduct (Repute).

10: You leave any part of the work with any member and never check whether they are doing it; what they take on gets done and what they promise about it holds.

1: You check up on and chase others' work and redo what they skimp, expecting them to shirk, cut corners or go back on their word.

Pre-language: Whether she can turn her back on them at a shared task. One who counts on her fellows leaves the watch, the carry or the young in their hands and goes about her own business without looking back; one who does not keeps glancing over, hovers at their work or takes it over herself. Intimates read it from how often she looks back, checks and takes over. The mechanism is trust calibrated to a partner's record of carrying a joint task, the kind of partner assessment the interdependence account places early in human cooperation (Tomasello et al. 2012). What sets this Pillar apart from Reciprocity is what the record is of: the partner's share of a joint task, not a favour returned to her. It is her reading of them; whether they turn their backs on her is a different thing and not read here.

Effect on Engagement: With competent and trustworthy people because you like being associated with 'winners', you admire and wish to model yourself off them, and they can help you to improve.

Parity (Levelling)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How far you feel no one in the group sets themselves over you: makes you do, drop or endure things by force or fear; takes more than the group's ordinary share-out gives them, of food, credit or say, and makes it stick; or tilts how shares, turns and chances are handed out, or how a quarrel is settled, towards themselves or their favourites, passing you over. You go along of your own accord, unafraid, not shortchanged and not passed over. It is not rank (Rank), acceptance (Belonging), deference for what you bring (Esteem), the return on help or whether those with a surplus of their own share it on demand (Reciprocity), whether others do their part of the work (Dependability), the cost of showing yourself (Safety) or the others' verdict on your own conduct (Repute). A respected leader, a settled order you accept, an even-handed share-out that happens to leave you less this time, or the group together pulling up a breach of its ways leaves it high; a member you must appease, one who grabs and gets away with it, or one who hands out or settles in favour of their own lowers it. Where the group has spoken ways of deciding, having those ways applied to you as to anyone, and a fair hearing for your say, feed the same reading even when the outcome goes against you; a say that is heard and then brushed aside, never weighed, does not raise it.

10: No member or clique can make you do or drop anything by force or threat, no one takes more than their due and keeps it, and whoever hands out or settles things does so with no thumb on the scale. You move, take your share and go about your business in the strongest member's presence as freely as in anyone's.

1: One or a few members make you comply through force or fear, take more than their due and keep it, or hand out and settle things in favour of their own while you are passed over. You watch them warily, fall quiet when they come near, and let them have their way to head off their anger, or because objecting gets you nowhere.

Pre-language: Freedom from a bully she must appease. The free animal moves, feeds and takes her share in the strongest member's presence without flinching or a glance at that member's mood; the coerced one tracks that member's moods, freezes on approach and does whatever heads off an attack. Intimates read it from whether she watches one particular member warily and shrinks or placates when that member comes near, while staying easy with everyone else, and whether, at a share-out, she is handed her portion in turn or watches the one dividing it feed his friends first and pass her by.

Safety (DivsExp)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How safe you feel to show yourself in this group: to let a slip, a mood, a need or a disagreement show, or go about things your own way, expecting no put-down, mockery or rebuff for it. It is your reading of what showing yourself will cost you, not whether you speak up, whether a need you show gets met (Reciprocity), whether your word carries weight (Esteem), whether you are wanted (Belonging), whether anyone pushes you about by force or fear (Parity), the verdict already held on your conduct (Repute), being openly charged or caught out before those who count (Face) or your own indignation at others' departures (Rule-Keeping).

10: You feel free to let slips, moods, needs and disagreements show as they come and to go about things your own way, expecting no one to pounce on them, laugh at them or turn away.

1: You feel that letting a slip, a mood, a plain need, a disagreement or a way of your own show would draw a put-down, so you scan faces before you move and keep your reactions masked.

Pre-language: Relaxed against braced among her own: the loose body and open play of an animal that expects no bite from its fellows, against the scanning, tense stillness of one that does. Intimates read it from how loose or tight she is when eyes turn to her, and from whether she hides a hurt or a want.

Effect on Engagement: Where you feel that your ideas will be welcomed and well-received. While related to IncResp (HCP), Expression is closer to a norm of Psychological Safety than being given specific respect for one's competence. Such a norm creates a warm, less hostile environment, which is distinct from cohesion: a close, friendly group can still make challenge feel risky.

Reciprocity

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

Your felt reading of whether help in this group comes back: what you give is returned, what you ask for is met. It holds until evidence moves it. It concerns the return on help, not whether others carry their part of shared work (Dependability), whether anyone takes more of a common take than their due (Parity), where you stand (Rank), whether the others want you among them (Belonging) or how they judge your conduct (Repute), though your name as a sharer (Repute) feeds the return. The culture's face sets where the return is looked for.

10: What you give comes back and what you ask for is met, as a matter of course; you count on the return without a second thought.

1: What you give is not returned and what you need goes unmet; you expect nothing back from anyone here.

Pre-language: The felt return on sharing: grooming that is returned by those groomed (Schino and Aureli 2008), and forager food handed over on demand to whoever asks (Peterson 1993), with those who have given tending to be given to in turn (Allen-Arave, Gurven and Hill 2008). Intimates read it as a sign in her behaviour: whether she hands over on request and asks as of right, expecting the return, or hesitates, hoards and goes without rather than ask.

Return from the group. Help goes to whoever needs it, and the return comes from the group at large, not only from the one helped. It is conditional on being seen to share, not on a strict tally: one seen to share is given to, one seen to hoard is passed over, and whoever has a surplus is pressed to share on demand. Return among foragers also tracks a particular partner's past giving (Allen-Arave, Gurven and Hill 2008; Jaeggi and Gurven 2013); that contingency is the hierarchical face working alongside. Your reading is whether, as one seen to share, you are given to by the group when you are in need. 10: Whoever has gives to whoever needs; what you have put in comes back to you from any member when you are in need. 1: Giving goes into a hole: nothing comes back from anyone, those with a surplus hide it, and need goes unmet.

Return from the partner. Help flows between particular partners who return it to each other. It is conditional on a return from the same partner: in kind between equals, or across rank, as favour and protection passed down for loyalty and service passed up. Your reading is whether your partners pay you back, not where you stand (Rank) or whether they do their part of the shared work (Dependability). 10: Every partner you help pays you back and those you ask deliver; whoever stands above you covers you and whoever stands below you backs you, each in turn. 1: Partners take and do not return; whoever stands above you leaves you uncovered and whoever stands below you will not back you; you expect no return from anyone you deal with.

Belonging

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How far you feel the others want you among them: whether they make room for you and draw you in, or leave you at the edge. It is their acceptance of you, read from how they treat you, not whether they defer to you for skill or contribution (Esteem), where you stand in the order (Rank) or how they judge your conduct (Repute). The culture's face sets what the acceptance rests on.

10: Others make room for you on sight and draw you into whatever is going on; you never doubt that you are wanted here.

1: Gatherings form without you and you are left at the edge; you doubt that anyone wants you here.

Pre-language: Being let into the huddle or kept out of it, time after time. The others shift to make a place, share, groom and turn towards her, or close ranks, turn away and leave her at the fringe, and keep doing so. Intimates read it from whether she moves freely into the middle of the group or hovers at its edge, watching for a gap.

Wanted as one of their own in good standing. The others want you among them as one of their own in good standing: you pull with the group as far as you are able and do not feed on it. The acceptance does not rise or fall with your output or with any place in an order, but it is not unconditional: a member the group has judged to shirk, cheat or feed on the others (Repute) is edged out. You read it from how the group as a whole treats you, not from the judgement itself. 10: Others make room for you and draw you in as a matter of course, and have done so through good seasons and bad; only shirking, cheating or turning on the group would change it. 1: Gatherings form without you and you are left at the edge: they treat you as a freeloader or an outsider, not as one of their own.

Included while you keep your place. The others keep you among them so long as you keep to what your place in the order calls for, high or low, and do not step out of line. The acceptance is real but conditional on keeping the place, not on the place itself (Rank). You read it from how they treat you while you keep it and from the standing threat of being dropped. 10: You have kept your place and the others keep you among them: at every gathering a place is made for you, whether high or low, as a matter of course. 1: You have stepped out of line and been dropped, or were never given a place at all: gatherings form without you and you are kept at the edge.

Esteem (Prestige)

Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional

How far the others defer to you freely for what you bring: they turn to you, watch and copy how you do it, bring you their problems and take your advice. It is not whether they want you among them (Belonging), your rung in the settled order (Rank) or their verdict on your conduct (Repute). The culture's face sets how far the deference reaches.

10: Whenever your kind of skill or contribution counts, the others turn to you, watch and copy how you do it, bring you their problems and take your advice.

1: No one asks you, watches you or copies you; when your kind of skill or contribution is needed they turn to someone else.

Pre-language: Being the one others watch, copy and seek out: eyes on her hands, bodies drawn near while she works, problems brought to her, her way of doing things taken up; as children attend to and learn from models whom others attend to. Intimates read it from who gets watched, copied and sought, and who is passed over when a task of her kind comes up.

Effect on Engagement: Where you feel that others have a high opinion of your competence and trustworthiness: you feel valued and understood; you feel that others regard you to be a legitimate and useful member of the group; your identity as belonging to this group is consistent with others' appraisal of you.

Looked to for what you bring, kept modest. How far you feel the others turn to you freely for what you bring the band: skill, knowledge, a good eye for the venture in hand. They watch how you do it, copy you, follow your lead on the matter in hand and bring you their problems, while you stay one of them: the deference gives you no right to command, and it lasts only while what you bring does. Whether you carry it modestly is the others' verdict on your conduct (Repute), which feeds it. Being shown up as clumsy or mistaken on a matter of skill, or as falling short on your share for want of skill rather than will, lowers it; falling short for want of will is Repute's ground. It is not whether they want you among them (Belonging), not freedom from being pushed about (Parity) and not the return on your help (Reciprocity). 10: Whenever your kind of skill counts, the others look to you, copy how you do it, bring you their problems and follow your lead on it for the day. 1: No one watches, copies or follows you on anything; when your kind of skill is needed they turn to someone else.

Deferred to for what you bring. How far you feel the others defer to you freely for what you bring the group: skill, knowledge or contribution it values. They watch how you do it, copy you, bring you problems, take your advice, hand you decisions and jobs that matter and take your word on them. The deference is given, not owed to any place in a rank order (Rank). Being handed a decision or a job because of what you bring is part of it; being shown up before others as clumsy or mistaken on a matter of skill, or as falling short on your share for want of skill rather than will, lowers it. Whether the others count you a decent member, fair in your dealings and carrying your share of the work, is not (Repute); nor is whether anyone of standing has openly charged you with, or caught you at, wronging people or dodging your share (Face); and neither is whether help you give comes back to you (Reciprocity). It fades once what you bring does; any precedence that has by then settled into your place is Rank, not Esteem. 10: Whenever your kind of skill or contribution counts, the others turn to you, watch and copy how you do it, bring you their problems and take your advice. 1: No one asks you, watches you or copies you; when your kind of skill or contribution is needed they turn to someone else.

Force cards

Making Fetch Happen: Belonging to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When the others draw me in as one of their own, and after a knock one of them comes and sits with me, my bracing eases; I expect a slip, a mood or a disagreement of mine to be taken as coming from one of their own, and my felt safety to show myself rises.

Decrement: When gatherings form without me and no one comes to me after a knock, I expect a slip or a disagreement of mine to be met as an outsider's would be, with a rebuff, and I mask myself and brace: my felt safety to show myself falls.

Consolation by a valued partner lowers stress behaviour in chimpanzees after aggression (Fraser, Stahl and Aureli 2008), and it is more likely between partners with valuable relationships; a member drawn in as one of their own has such partners to come to her. A member who is wanted expects her exposure to be borne as one of their own; one left at the edge expects it to be held against her. Felt safety in teams is a shared reading that interpersonal risk is acceptable (Edmondson 1999).

Pre-language (increment): When others seek her out and play with her, she lets her moods and fumbles show without watching faces.

Pre-language (decrement): When others leave her at the edge, she watches faces, masks her reactions and braces for a snap.

Friends at my back: Belonging to Levelling (Reinforce, E)

Generated for the draft model; provisional, awaiting Ben Rechecked 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars: kept.

Increment: When I feel the others want me among them, I sense they would close round me if anyone tried to push me about, and my sense that no one can lord it over me rises.

Decrement: When gatherings form without me and no one seeks me out, I feel I would stand alone if someone pushed me about, and my sense that no one can lord it over me falls.

Felt protection from domination rests on expected coalitional support, and being bonded into the group is the felt basis of that expectation; an isolated member is exposed. Elaboration: when the low reading comes from being shut out, her reaction may show hostility, aimed readily at whoever she deals with next, even someone who has done nothing to her, and withheld only from those who treat her warmly (Twenge, Baumeister, Tice and Stucke 2001); if the exclusion is public and stands as an open charge that she wronged someone or let the group down on her share, the Reputation expansion (Face) carries that flare.

Pre-language (increment): When others seek her out and groom her, she faces a swaggering member without shrinking, expecting her companions to come to her side, and her sense of no bully rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When others leave her on her own, she shrinks when a forceful member nears, with no one to run to, and her sense of no bully sinks.

One of us, so it comes back: Belonging to Reciprocity (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When the others draw me in as one of their own, I feel surer that what I put in will come back from the group and that what I need will be met: my sense that help comes back to me rises.

Decrement: When gatherings form without me and I am left at the edge, I feel that what I give goes into a hole and that my needs would go unmet: my sense that help comes back to me falls.

In the return-from-the-group face, help goes to whoever in the group needs it, and someone the others treat as an outsider stands outside that giving. Being wanted as one of their own in good standing is the felt sign that she is among those the group's giving reaches, so her need will be met; being left at the edge is the sign that she stands outside that reach and will be passed over. Her name as a sharer is a separate route (Bad Name, Empty Hands). People expect generalised returns from their own group and not from outsiders (bounded generalised reciprocity: Yamagishi and Kiyonari 2000); carrying that from group membership to graded acceptance within one group is an extension, so keep the step modest.

Pre-language (increment): When others seek her out and draw her in, she reaches for a share of what they have without hesitation, expecting it to be handed over, and her sense that giving comes back grows.

Pre-language (decrement): When others leave her at the edge, she hangs back from the food and holds what she has close, expecting nothing to come her way, and her sense that giving comes back sinks.

Open or masked: DivsExp to Belonging (Discretionary, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (second round); provisional

Whether feeling safe to show myself draws the others closer depends on what I would be showing them. Circumstance one: what shows is ordinary, moods, owned slips and disagreements aired for the group's sake. HIGH: I let them show, the others read me as one of their own and draw me in, so my Belonging rises. LOW: braced and masked, I come across as aloof, and they leave me at the edge of the talk, so my Belonging falls. Circumstance two: what I have to show is mostly a run of needs, complaints and pleas for reassurance, pressed on the others more often than they can comfortably carry, and they have begun to tire of it. HIGH: I go on letting them show, I wear on them, and they edge away a little, so my Belonging falls. LOW: braced and masked, I keep those needs to myself; nothing new is laid on them, but masking also cools their warmth towards me, so my Belonging holds where it is. Someone already wanted among them is borne with longer, and needs she cannot help are borne as one of their own. Whether they judge her to be feeding on them is Repute's ground, carried by Can't Look Them in the Eye. Masked expression lowers a partner's rapport and wish to affiliate (Butler et al. 2003), and disclosure draws liking (Collins and Miller 1994), for circumstance one.

Pre-language (explanation): When she does her share alongside the others, showing her moods and fumbles freely draws them to her, while going still and masked leaves her on the edge. When the others have begun to turn from her constant wants and complaints, showing more of them makes them turn further away, while keeping them hidden lets them come back to her and make room for her again.

Mistakes in the open: DivsExp to GrpProsp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When I feel safe to let a slip or a disagreement show, I sense that troubles with the venture come out where the group can deal with them, and I feel surer it can pull the venture off.

Decrement: When I brace and mask myself, I sense that slips and doubts are being hidden around me as well as by me, and I feel less sure the group can pull the venture off.

Psychological safety supports team learning behaviour, through which teams take up problems and correct course; in Edmondson's (1999) teams it worked on performance through that learning behaviour. Edmondson measured safety as a belief the team shares. A member's own felt safety is one sign of whether that climate holds around her, so it carries into her confidence in the group's capability. Her sense that others hide their slips too is an inference from her own masking, so keep the step modest.

Pre-language (increment): When she is loose among them and her fumbles on the shared venture draw help rather than jeers, she sees fumbles mended as they happen and goes at the venture with confidence.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is braced and hides her fumbles, she sees others hide theirs too, and the venture feels shakier to her.

Free to scoff, free of bullies: DivsExp to Levelling (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When I feel safe to let a disagreement show, I bristle or scoff at anyone who starts to push me about, help themselves to more than their due, or tilt a share-out or a turn towards themselves or their favourites, and when others take up my scoff the move is checked: I feel no one here could set themselves over me without an answer from us, and my sense of Parity rises.

Decrement: When I brace and mask myself, I let a pushy member's demands, grabs and favouritism pass without a murmur and take what is handed to me, and I feel myself made to go along: my sense of Parity falls.

The everyday tools of levelling are ridicule, criticism and open objection, and they bite when they are collective: among the Ju/'hoansi, humorous put-downs of big-shot behaviour escalate to harsh criticism and withheld sharing (Wiessner 2005), and followers acting together check would-be dominants (Boehm 1993). A member who feels safe to let a disagreement show is free to use these tools against a pushy member; that she does so rests on common sense, since the safety in question is safety to object. Where others take them up, force, grabbing and favouritism lose their grip on her. A lone scoff that no one takes up does not check a dominant, so set the increment small where the others stay silent; expected backing is carried by E:Belonging->Levelling. Both lines need someone pushing, grabbing or tilting a share-out: where no member is doing so, masking leaves nothing to let pass, so set the decrement small or nil. The favouritism limb follows Q5: preschoolers protest an unequal split more when a rigged procedure produced it than when a fair one did (Grocke, Rossano and Tomasello 2015).

Pre-language (increment): When she is loose among the others, she bristles, mocks or protests when a swaggering member pushes at her, and goes about her business beside him without a glance at his mood.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is braced, she goes still and gives way when a swaggering member pushes at her, and watches his mood.

No cover-ups: DivsExp to OutResp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When I feel safe to let my own slips show, I take it that no one here needs to dress up a report, so when a member says a part is done I take it as done and leave it in their hands: my confidence that they will do their part rises.

Decrement: When I brace and mask my own slips, I take it that the others dress up their reports as I would, so 'done' no longer means done and I check what they say they have finished: my confidence that they will do their part falls.

Where showing a slip draws a put-down, members cover their shortfalls, and raising problems goes with felt safety (Edmondson 1999; cross-sectional, so the direction is not established). In an unsafe group, then, a report that work is done cannot be taken at face value. Caution: in a small study of eight hospital units, more open units reported more detected errors (Edmondson 1996, Journal of Applied Behavioral Science 32), so in a safe group she also hears of more slips. Dependability moves here with whether reports can be trusted; the count of slips she hears of is a separate matter. A run of owned and fixed slips reads as reliability, and a run of unfixed ones belongs on a Dependability evidence card. The step from her own safety to her reading of others' reports rests on common sense: people judge others' candour by their own, and safety is a climate members share, so a member who need not hide her slips expects that the others need not hide theirs. No checked source tests that step, so keep the card modest.

Pre-language (increment): When she is loose among them and shows her own fumbles, she leaves a shared task in another's hands and turns away without looking back.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is braced and hides her own fumbles, she keeps glancing back at a shared task left with another, and goes over it herself.

Need shown, need met: DivsExp to Reciprocity (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When I feel safe to let a need show, I let it show, and seeing it met I feel surer that what I put into this group comes back.

Decrement: When I brace and keep my needs masked, I only hint at them; the hints go unnoticed and nothing comes: my sense that what I put into this group comes back falls.

Felt safety lets a member show her needs, and the help that answers them confirms the return. A braced member only hints at hers. Hints are easy to miss, so nothing comes, and the shortfall lowers her sense of return; both steps rest on common sense. People underestimate how readily others help when asked directly (Flynn and Lake 2008). A need shown plainly is the nearest thing to a direct request, so a member who shows one may be met more often than she expects, while one who masks it never learns her estimate was too low. The study used direct requests among strangers; carrying it to shown needs in a standing group is an extension, so keep both lines modest, and keep the decrement small where she has not hinted at a need at all.

Pre-language (increment): When she is loose among them, she whimpers or reaches when hungry or hurt, is given to, and her sense that giving comes back grows.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is braced, she hides her hunger or hurt, is given nothing, and her sense that giving comes back sinks.

Reading the welcome through my own warmth: Engagement to Belonging (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When this group feels part of who I am, the small signs (a nod, a seat kept, a glance my way) read to me as welcome for one of their own, and my sense that they want me among them rises.

Decrement: When I am pulling out of this group, the same small signs read as mere politeness and the gaps read as edging me out, as if I were an outsider, and my sense that they want me among them falls.

Most belonging cues in a small group are ambiguous, and people read them in line with how they themselves stand. The sociometer gauges felt relational value from such cues (Leary and Baumeister 2000), and people who anxiously expect rejection readily perceive it in others' behaviour (Downey and Feldman 1996, a disposition studied in romantic partners). Those works concern expectation, not investment, so the step from her own investment to that reading is a proposal on common sense. A person for whom the group is part of who she is gives the others the benefit of the doubt. A person on her way out reads coolness into the same scene, and finds in it a felt reason for going. Her own investment colours how she reads their acceptance of her as one of their own; how they judge her conduct is Repute's ground, and the card moves only her reading of the others' treatment, not the treatment itself.

Pre-language (increment): Bound up in the band, she takes the others' approaches and the room made beside her as welcome. Her feeling of being wanted among them rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Drifting away from the band, she reads the others' glances as indifferent and sees groups forming without her. Her feeling of being wanted among them falls.

Bringing herself in, or bracing: Engagement to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When this group is part of who I am, I bring my whole self into it, and the faces around me read as open rather than judging: I feel safer letting slips, moods, needs and disagreements show.

Decrement: When I have withdrawn into myself and am on my way out of this group, the same faces read as watchful and ready to mock: I mask my reactions, braced for a put-down, and feel less safe to let them show.

Kahn (1990) defines engagement and disengagement as two movements of the self, expressing it in the role or withdrawing and defending it, and names safety as one condition of engagement. The established path therefore runs from safety to engagement; a meta-analysis of psychological safety places engagement in its network as an outcome (Frazier et al. 2017; mostly cross-sectional studies). The feedback path here is a proposal. Investment carries enthusiasm and withdrawal carries flatness, and mood colours judgements of other people in its own direction (Forgas 1995, checked only in part), so an invested member may read the same faces as more open and a withdrawing one as more watchful. Kahn's account does not itself show how a withdrawing member reads faces; that step rests on the mood route alone. Keep the card smaller than Safety's evidence cards. I considered Inverse (an invested member has more to lose, so feels more exposed) but rejected it as the default, because Kahn treats self-expression and engagement as one movement; that exposure effect belongs on a scene card about how a shown disagreement is received.

Pre-language (increment): Bound up in the band, she moves loosely and plays unguarded, and eyes turning to her no longer feel like a threat: her felt safety among them rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Withdrawn from the band, she tightens, scans faces and goes still, and eyes turning to her feel like a coming blow: her felt safety among them falls.

Thrown in, the venture looks winnable: Engagement to GrpProsp (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When I am thrown into this group heart and effort, I feel buoyed, and what we manage feels like a sign of what we can do: I feel more sure that we, as we stand, can pull off the venture we have taken on.

Decrement: When I have withdrawn from this group and am half out of the door, I feel flat, and the same showing looks like the limit of what we can do: I feel less sure that we, as we stand, can pull off the venture we have taken on.

Her own investment carries a feeling (enthusiasm or flatness), and that feeling seeps unbidden into her reading of the group's capability for the venture still ahead. The Affect Infusion Model describes the route: mood colours judgements she builds from scratch, whether by quick heuristics or by working them through, and colours least those she simply recalls or makes with a set aim in view (Forgas 1995). Salanova, Llorens and Schaufeli (2011) propose and test a gain spiral in which efficacy beliefs and engagement influence each other over time through positive affect such as enthusiasm, in teachers and in students working in groups; the return path from engagement to efficacy was not confirmed in detail, so the loop from engagement to felt prospects is a likely reading of their work and should be kept modest. Most of that evidence concerns a member's belief in her own capability; its spread to the group's capability is less directly tested. Because Team Confidence also feeds Engagement, the two form a positive loop; the brake must come from Team Confidence evidence cards (setbacks, missed goals), and the increment here should be modest.

Pre-language (increment): Bound up in the band's shared push, she moves with spring, and the venture ahead looks within the band's reach: her sense of the band's prospects rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Withdrawn and hanging back, she sees the band fumble, and the venture ahead looks beyond it: her sense of the band's prospects falls.

Inside the coalition: Engagement to Levelling (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When this group is part of who I am, it feels like ours to defend, and I feel ready to stand with the rest against anyone who throws their weight about; a forceful member no longer looks able to make me do or drop anything, or to take more than their due and keep it: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me rises.

Decrement: When I have drawn back from this group but cannot readily leave it, it no longer feels worth a stand, and I would sooner keep my head down than face anyone down; a forceful member looms larger and I give way to their mood: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me falls.

In forager bands, the absence of a bully rests on a levelling coalition of the rest, ready to check a would-be dominant (Boehm 1993). Boehm describes the coalition at the level of the band; the model takes her felt freedom from being pushed about to depend partly on her own readiness to join that check, a step resting on common sense. Among employees, greater satisfaction and investment go with voice and loyalty, and lesser with exit and neglect (Rusbult and colleagues 1988); that work concerns responses to a declining job, so its extension to standing up to a forceful member is the model's. When Engagement is high the group feels like hers to defend, so a forceful member feels less able to make her comply. When it is low and she cannot readily leave, nothing here seems worth a stand, and the same forcefulness feels like a threat she must appease. Caution, on common sense: a member with a ready and cheap way out depends less on the group and has less to lose by defying a forceful member, so set the decrement small or nil where her exit is ready. Whether the others would back her is a separate matter, carried by Friends at my back (Belonging). Parity here is her own felt exposure to force, fear or a grab that sticks, and leaves aside whether she likes or rates the forceful member.

Pre-language (increment): Drawn into the band, she stands among the others when a forceful member swaggers, feels them at her side and goes on with her business. Her sense that no one can push her about rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Pulled to the band's edge, she watches the forceful member warily, goes still when it comes near and gives way, feeling no one at her back. Her sense that no one can push her about falls.

Trusting those I am in it with: Engagement to OutResp (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When I am thrown into this group, I read the others warmly, and the way they carry their part looks dependable: I feel more confident that they will do what they take on.

Decrement: When I have withdrawn from this group, I read the others coolly, and a task let drop weighs more with me than the ones carried through: I feel less confident that they will do what they take on.

Two routes. Mood congruence acts in the moment: on common sense, being thrown into a group goes with a warmer mood and drawing back with a cooler one, and mood colours judgements of other people, including quick ones of whether they will keep their word (Forgas 1995). The affect infusion model predicts less infusion when she judges with a set aim in view (motivated processing), as she may when a teammate she depends on must deliver, so keep the card modest. Sampling adds a slower effect over many plays: an engaged member keeps relying on others, so a single let-down is soon corrected by tasks carried through; a disengaged member stops relying on them, so the last let-down stands as the verdict (Denrell 2005). The card moves reliability only, leaving her reading of the group's capability to Team Confidence. One caution: members who believe a partner is not pulling their weight cut their own effort (the sucker effect, Kerr 1983). That reaction is driven by seeing the coasting, so it belongs on a Dependability evidence card, not here.

Pre-language (increment): Bound up in the band, she leaves tasks in others' hands and sees them done, and each task carried through sticks: her trust that those around her will do their part rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Withdrawn from the band, she stops leaving tasks with others, and the last task dropped is what she carries away: her trust that they will do their part falls.

One of us, so paid back: Engagement to Reciprocity (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When this group is part of who I am, I pour my time and effort into it, I feel the others need what I bring, and what comes my way reads as the group looking after one it relies on: my sense that help here comes back to me rises.

Decrement: When I am pulling out of this group, I know I have been holding back my time and effort and have given the others less reason to look after me, so when I am in need I expect to be passed over: my sense that help here comes back to me falls.

In egalitarian sharing the return comes from the group. When members depend on one another, each has a direct stake in a partner's welfare and helps that partner (Roberts 2005; Tomasello and colleagues 2012); both are theoretical evolutionary accounts, and their extension to a member's felt Engagement in a present-day group is the model's. Engagement is the felt size of her stake and effort in the group. When it is high she feels the others need what she brings, counts herself someone they have reason to help, and reads ambiguous cues of others' giving as return for what she has put in. When it is low she knows she has held back, feels she has given them less reason to look after her, and expects to be passed over. The reading of ambiguous cues and the expectation of being passed over rest on common sense. Whether the others want her among them is a separate route (One of us, so it comes back), and so is what they say of her as a sharer (Bad Name, Empty Hands). The card moves her reading of the group's return; it keeps no tally of particular debts.

Pre-language (increment): Bound up in the band, she shares freely and feels the band's food and help come round to her in turn. Her sense that what she gives comes back rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Loosened from the band, she keeps to herself and, when hungry, hangs back expecting nothing to be passed her way. Her sense that what she gives comes back falls.

Circle the Wagons: GrpProsp to Belonging (Discretionary, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (second round); provisional

Whether the venture's prospects draw the others round her depends on where the trouble is seen to come from. Threats seen as external tend to strengthen group identity, and threats seen as internal can weaken it (Greenaway and Cruwys 2019, a theoretical synthesis). Circumstance one (the default): the trouble is seen as inside the group, or no source is named. HIGH: with the venture going well, the others are easy with each other and with her and draw her in, so her Belonging rises (runs as Reinforce). LOW: with the venture failing, the others grow short with each other and she is left at the edge of the talk, so her Belonging falls. The stronger path may run from performance to cohesion (Mullen and Copper 1994), but the effect is small, comes from results where Team Confidence is a forecast, and runs mainly through commitment to the task, with liking among members playing a smaller part, so keep this branch modest. In the egalitarian face acceptance holds through good seasons and bad, so keep it smallest for a member long drawn in. Being blamed herself for the failure is Repute's ground (Pointing Fingers), not this card's. Circumstance two: the trouble is seen as coming from outside (a rival group, an outside body, or a setback from outside such as lost funding or a forced change of ground), and the group still sees a fight worth making. LOW here means the venture is threatened, not yet hopeless: the others close ranks against the threat and draw her in as one of us, so her Belonging rises (runs as Inverse). HIGH: the outside threat looks easily met, the huddle loosens and her place returns to its ordinary level, so her Belonging slips back down, by no more than an earlier huddle raised it; with no such rise, the step is nil. External conflict raises cohesion only under some conditions (Stein 1976). On common sense the model takes those conditions to include a threat that falls on all of them and a joint effort that seems able to meet it, so where the venture looks hopeless, run circumstance one.

Pre-language (explanation): Where the band huddles when things go badly and she is still half an outsider, a faltering venture has them gathering close and pulling her in among them, while a venture going well lets them drift back to leaving her on the edge. Where the band turns on whoever seems to drag, a faltering venture may leave her at the edge, while a venture going well sees them make room for her again.

Stakes tighten or loosen: GrpProsp to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When I feel sure the group can pull off the venture, no one is hunting for whose slip will cost us, so a slip passes without remark and I let my tiredness, moods and doubts show, expecting no one to pounce: my sense that I can show myself here without cost rises.

Decrement: When I feel the venture is beyond us, I feel heads turning to find who is dragging us down, so I mask my tiredness and keep my doubts and disagreements hidden, braced for blame: my sense that I can show myself here without cost falls.

A change in the venture's prospects changes how much seems to hang on each member's showing. With the rowing crew's season looking won there is slack, no one hunts for a culprit, and a doubt about the stroke passes as a refinement. With the season looking lost, heads turn to find whose slip is costing the crew and she masks her tiredness, braced for a put-down. The card carries only that anticipated cost of showing herself, before any charge is made; a charge of shirking made openly by someone of standing is Face's ground, and the group's verdict that she does not pull her weight is Repute's, carried by Pointing Fingers. The link from failing prospects to a hunt for culprits rests on common sense. Threat rigidity (Staw, Sandelands and Dutton 1981), a broad theory with thin group-level tests, points the same way but awaits a check and is not relied on, so keep the card modest. Where a group treats errors as things to learn from and fix, with no punishment, felt safety goes with learning behaviour (Edmondson 1999, one firm, cross-sectional), so set the decrement small or nil there. Caution on the high side: in a tight-knit group whose confidence has hardened, a doubt about the plan itself can draw pressure to keep quiet. That point also rests on common sense; groupthink, often cited for it, has only partial empirical support (Esser 1998) and is not relied on. Set the increment small for disagreement in such a group. The card runs as Reinforce; no reverse effect is strong enough to make it Discretionary.

Pre-language (explanation): Where the band's way is to try other ways when things go badly, a faltering venture draws them together and she shows her moods and fumbles freely, while a venture going well has them guarding what works and she keeps her fumbles hidden, bracing a little. Where the band's way is to turn on one another, a faltering venture makes her go still, watch faces and mask her reactions, while a venture going well leaves no one turning on anyone and she moves unguarded again.

Failing hunts breed bosses: GrpProsp to Levelling (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When I feel sure the group can pull off the venture, I see no call for anyone to take charge by force or settle things over our heads, and if the strongest starts to drive the pace the rest of us shrug it off; I go about my business beside them without a glance at their mood: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me rises.

Decrement: When I feel the venture is beyond us, I feel the rest of us looking to the strongest to take charge, and when they drive us by threat and temper and settle things without hearing us, no one pushes back and I find myself doing what they want to head off their anger: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me falls.

When people feel a loss of control under uncertainty they turn towards dominant leaders over prestigious ones (Kakkar and Sivanathan 2017, large cross-national samples from 69 countries; their uncertainty was economic and personal, so its extension to a failing group venture is a proposal). A failing venture may therefore lend a would-be dominant the support that would otherwise check him. Threat rigidity (Staw, Sandelands and Dutton 1981) proposes that threat centralises control; it awaits a check and is not relied on here. On the high side, on common sense, members confident of success see no need for anyone to take charge, so a would-be dominant who tries to drive the pace is shrugged off. Direction that rests on force, or that settles things without a hearing, lowers a member's Parity; a respected leader simply taking the lead would not. The increment should be modest.

Pre-language (increment): When the band's venture is going well, no one shoves or snaps, and if the strongest starts to, the others ignore him; she goes about her business beside him without a glance at his mood, and her sense that no one can push her about rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When the venture is faltering, the strongest start shoving and snapping, and she goes still near them and does what they want to head off their anger, and her sense that no one can push her about falls.

Scapegoating: GrpProsp to OutResp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When the group's venture looks well within its reach, I credit the others with carrying their parts, and I feel I can leave work in their hands without checking: my confidence that they will do their part rises.

Decrement: When the venture looks beyond the group, my frustration looks for whose shirking or broken word is dragging it down, and I come to expect that member, and others like them, to let their parts slip: my confidence that the others will do their part falls.

A venture that looks within reach casts a warm light on the others' carrying-through, so she leaves work in their hands with less checking; this step rests on common sense, so keep the increment modest. One that looks beyond the group can set her looking for a culprit, and some of the blame may land on a member's unwillingness. Blame that lands on a member's want of skill moves Team Confidence or Esteem, not this card. Members' attributions for a group's outcome shift with its success or failure (Forsyth and Schlenker 1977). The further claims that members lay more of a failure on one another than on themselves (Schlenker and Miller 1977), and that observers credit a team for success but lay its failure on individual members (Naquin and Tynan 2003), are not yet checked. Those studies concern failure already suffered; the step to a felt forecast of failure is a proposal, so keep the decrement modest. Where the group lays the failure on an outside cause instead, no member is blamed, and the decrement should be small.

Pre-language (increment): When the venture is going well, she watches those carrying it with approval and leaves them to their tasks without hovering.

Pre-language (decrement): When it is going badly, her frustration turns on whoever faltered: she glares at them, hovers over what they do and snatches tasks back from them.

Leaned on, left out: Levelling to Belonging (Reinforce, E)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When no one in the group can push me about or take what is mine, and whoever hands out shares or settles a quarrel does it even-handedly, I move among the others freely and nothing keeps me at the edge when they gather: my sense that they want me among them rises a little.

Decrement: When a forceful member makes me comply through fear, I go quiet and keep out of the way at gatherings, and the others, wary of the one who leans on me, keep their distance too; or when whoever hands out shares or settles a quarrel passes me over for his own and the rest let it stand, I take it that I count for less among them. Either way the circle tends to form without me: my sense that they want me among them falls.

A member pushed about by force or fear draws back from the group's circle: she keeps out of the way of the one who leans on her, and so is less often among the others. This rests on common sense about avoiding a threat. Whether the others also pull away from her is unsettled: among children, victimisation by peers is reported to predict growing rejection (Hodges and Perry 1999, not yet checked), and carrying that to adult groups would be a further extension, so keep the step modest. Partial dealing is a second route, since Parity covers share-outs and settlements as well as force: when whoever hands out shares or settles a quarrel passes her over and the rest let it stand, she reads it as a sign that she counts for less among them. The relational model of procedural justice holds that people read even-handed treatment by those in charge as a sign that they are valued members of the group, and partial treatment as a sign that they are not (Tyler and Lind 1992, not yet checked). Where no one can lord it over her and dealing is even, nothing holds her at the edge, since the others check a would-be dominant together (Boehm 1993); that removes a barrier without itself making her welcome, so set the increment smaller than the decrement. Ribbing a member who gets above herself is not this card: it is Repute's ground (Tall Poppy Talk; Insulting the meat).

Pre-language (explanation): After she brings in a large kill and carries herself high, where no one can push anyone about the others run down her meat, mock and turn their backs a little, and she feels less welcome until she lowers herself; where a strong one already pushes her about and turns on her for it, the others close round her and she feels more welcome. When she has done nothing to stand out and no one can drive her off, the others close round her when a strong one tries, and she feels more welcome; when a strong one already has her cowed, she keeps out of the way, the others stay clear of her, and she feels less welcome.

No blow to brace for: Levelling to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When no one here can make me do anything by force or threat, I stop watching for a blow and let my slips, moods and disagreements show as they come: my felt safety to show myself rises.

Decrement: When a member can make me comply through fear, I check his face before I move and keep my reactions masked, expecting any slip or disagreement of mine to draw his scorn or a put-down: my felt safety to show myself falls.

In social primates, scratching and other self-directed behaviour appear in socially tense situations and track anxiety (Troisi 2002); the claim that they rise specifically near a higher-ranking animal (Castles, Whiten and Aureli 1999) awaits checking. In despotic species subordination carries the heaviest stress, though not in egalitarian ones, and the pattern varies with species and with the stability of the hierarchy (Sapolsky 2005). In people, on common sense, the same guardedness shows as masking: near someone who can hurt her, she hides whatever might set him off, and when the threat is absent she shows herself. Team structures shape felt psychological safety (Edmondson 1999). Caution: the card runs through force or fear. Where her Parity is low only because someone takes more than their due, or hands out and settles in favour of his own, with no threat behind it, she has no blow to brace for, so set the decrement small.

Pre-language (increment): When no one looms over her, she plays and moves loosely, unguarded when eyes turn to her, and her ease at being seen rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When one member looms over her, she scans him, scratches herself and goes still as he nears, hiding any fumble, and her ease at being seen sinks.

Cowed hands: Levelling to GrpProsp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When no one here can make me do anything by force or fear, take more than their due, or hand things out to their own, I see my effort and the others' go into the venture itself rather than into watching one member's mood: my sense that the group can pull it off rises.

Decrement: When a member makes me comply through fear, takes more than his due and keeps it, or hands out the jobs and the shares to his own, I see my effort and the others' go into heading him off rather than into the venture: my sense that the group, as it stands, can pull off the venture sinks.

Coercion and partiality pull attention and effort away from the task and towards the one who holds them; that the lost effort weakens the venture rests on common sense. Chimpanzee pairs low in tolerance do worse at a cooperative task than tolerant pairs (Melis, Hare and Tomasello 2006a), and an abusive supervision climate lowers group performance through collective efficacy (Priesemuth et al. 2014, a cross-sectional field study; extended here from supervisor to any member, so keep the step modest). No checked source ties partiality in handing out jobs and shares to the group's capability, so where Parity is low only through favouritism, set the decrement small. Accepted differences of role and rank are not low Parity: differentiated hierarchy can help coordination on interdependent work (Halevy, Chou and Galinsky 2011; Ronay et al. 2012), and this card reads only coercion, grabbing and partiality. Pressure from members to make everyone pull their weight is not coercion in this sense. The card reads only the capability left to the venture; whether each member still does their part is Bullies poison trust (E:Levelling->OutResp), and problems or know-how kept quiet travel through Safety.

Pre-language (increment): When no one looms over the band, she sees them all intent on the chase or the forage, each putting in freely, and her feeling that it will come off rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When one member looms and snaps, she sees the band glancing at him rather than at the quarry, hanging back and breaking off, and her feeling that it will come off sinks.

Bullies poison trust: Levelling to OutResp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When no one here can make me do anything by force or fear, the others have no one to perform for, so how they carry their parts shows plainly and I check up on them less: my confidence that they will do their part rises a little.

Decrement: When a member here makes me comply through fear, I see the others work to please him rather than to finish their parts, cover themselves and let tasks drop once his eye moves on, and I start checking up on their work: my confidence that they will do their part falls.

Coercion distorts how others behave: they appease, hide, protect themselves and work to the coercer's eye, and she reads all of this as unreliable. On common sense, compliance won by threat holds while the one who wields it is watching, so she sees parts done for his eye and dropped when it moves on. The surveillance point (Kelman 1958; French and Raven 1959) and the finding that abused subordinates hold back discretionary effort and turn to deviance (Zellars, Tepper and Duffy 2002; Mitchell and Ambrose 2007) await checking; the card extends the latter from supervisor to any member. Hierarchy raises conflict-enabling states in teams (Greer et al. 2018), which fits the decrement only loosely. Without coercion this distortion is gone and the others' carrying-through shows plainly, but shirking can persist for other reasons, so keep the increment small. The card runs on force or fear only; where Parity is low only because someone grabs or hands out to their own, set it nil.

Pre-language (increment): When no one bullies, she watches the others keep at their tasks and leaves them to it without hovering: her sense that they will do their part rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When a bully dominates, she sees the others cringe, scramble for favour and abandon tasks as he passes, and she hovers over what they do: her sense that they will do their part falls.

No grabber, open hands: Levelling to Reciprocity (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When no one here can take what they like from me by force or threat, and no one takes more than their due and keeps it, nothing I share is seized on the way or turned into leverage over me, so it goes where it is needed and the others share back openly: my reading that help comes back rises.

Decrement: When a member can make me hand over what I have through fear, or helps himself to more than his due and gets away with it, what I put in goes to him as tribute and never back round the group, the others hide what they have, and I expect little back from anyone: my reading that help comes back falls.

Return from the group fares best where no one can seize what is shared or turn a gift into leverage. Immediate-return foragers act to prevent accumulation and domination (Woodburn 1982), and the rank and file check would-be dominants together (Boehm 1993). Sharing there runs largely on demand (Peterson 1993): claims pressed among equals are high Parity, and only a dominant's taking, backed by force or threat, counts as seizure here. The reverse case has indirect support at most: in a trust game, an investor who used a threat of fines is reported to have got less back than one who held it in reserve (Fehr and Rockenbach 2003, not yet checked). That finding comes from pairs of strangers, so carrying it to a group is an extension. The rest rests on common sense: under a coercer, giving becomes tribute, the others keep what they have out of his reach, and the return from the group dries up.

Pre-language (increment): When no one in the band looms or snatches, she gives from her pile and finds others giving from theirs when she is short, and her sense that what she gives comes back rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When one member snatches and threatens, what she holds out is taken and nothing comes back, the others hunch over their food, and her sense that giving brings any return sinks.

Don’t Dis Me Bro: OutResp to Belonging (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When I leave work in others' hands without checking, they read it as trust, answer in kind and work with me more readily: my sense that they want me among them rises.

Decrement: When I check up on, chase and redo others' work, they read it as distrust, draw back from me and work with me less readily: my sense that they want me among them falls.

Trust tends to be answered in kind. In dyads working together over time, each side's perceived trustworthiness and cooperation fed the other's in a spiral (Ferrin, Bligh and Kohles 2008), though reviews of dyadic trust warn that it is not always mutual (Korsgaard, Brower and Lester 2015). A member who leaves work in others' hands shows trust they can see, and they answer with trust and cooperation of their own. Control read as distrust lowers the controlled party's effort (Falk and Kosfeld 2006), real but usually small on replication (Ziegelmeyer, Schmelz and Ploner 2012). Neither source measures liking or inclusion. The step from how readily they work with her to her Belonging is common sense: being cooperated with is the plainest sign of being wanted. Keep the card small, and set the decrement smaller still where checking is the group's custom rather than her own choice.

Pre-language (increment): When she leaves others to their tasks without hovering, they warm to her and seek her company.

Pre-language (decrement): When she hovers over their work and snatches it back to redo it, they bristle, cool towards her and keep away.

Nobody hunting for cover: OutResp to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When the others carry through what they take on and keep their word, no one has failures of their own to cover with mine, so I expect my slips to be passed over and let them show: my felt safety to show myself rises.

Decrement: When the others shirk, cut corners and go back on their word, I expect them to seize on any slip of mine to cover their own, so I mask my slips and keep my reactions out of sight: my felt safety to show myself falls.

Where members fail to carry their parts, failures pile up, and it is common sense that those who dropped them look to shift the blame. Blame also spreads: people who watch someone blame another are more likely to blame others for their own unrelated failures, through a goal of protecting their self-image, and self-affirmation removes the effect (Fast and Tiedens 2010). A member in a group where parts are dropped can then expect her own visible slips to become someone's cover, and she masks them. Where everyone carries their part there is less failure to account for and less blame in the air, and showing herself costs little. The step from blame in the group to her felt safety is a proposal; keep the card modest. It is distinct from E:Parity->Safety (fear of one coercer) and E:Team Confidence->Safety (the stakes of the venture).

Pre-language (increment): When those around her do their share, she is loose and unguarded under their eyes when she fumbles.

Pre-language (decrement): When those around her slack off, she braces when she fumbles, expecting their glares and snarls to turn on her.

Quality Street: OutResp to GrpProsp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When I feel the others will carry through what they take on, I count every member's skill as put to work on the venture, with none of our effort lost to chasing or redoing parts: my confidence that the group, as it stands, can pull it off rises.

Decrement: When I expect the others to shirk, cut corners or go back on their word, I count on skill that will sit idle and on effort lost to chasing and redoing their parts, so the capability left for the venture shrinks: my confidence that the group, as it stands, can pull it off falls.

A joint venture depends on each part being carried through as well as on skill, so felt reliability feeds the sense of what the group, as it stands, can do. Intrateam trust is positively related to team performance across 112 studies (rho about .30), holding after past performance is controlled, and more so where tasks are interdependent (De Jong, Dirks and Gillespie 2016); team efficacy itself tracks performance more closely under high interdependence (Gully et al. 2002). The data are correlational and her forecast is a reading, so keep the card moderate, and smaller in loosely coupled groups where members can finish their work alone.

Pre-language (increment): When those around her keep at their tasks and finish what they start, she settles into the shared venture confident it will come off.

Pre-language (decrement): When those around her drift off and leave tasks half done, she grows uneasy about the shared venture, expecting it to fail.

Help binds us: Reciprocity to Belonging (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When what I give comes back from the others and what I need is met, I count them as people I cannot do without; after a clash I go back to them soon and make it up, they take me back, and the circle closes round me again: my Belonging rises.

Decrement: When what I give goes unreturned and my needs go unmet, I have little to lose with them; after a clash I stay away and let it stand, and the rift stays open: my Belonging falls.

The lines rest on reconciliation, the better evidenced route. Primates reconcile most with partners whose relationship is valuable to them, and raising partner value experimentally raises reconciliation (Cords and Thurnheer 1993; Aureli, Cords and van Schaik 2002); friendly reunions after a clash lower the risk of renewed attack (Aureli and van Schaik 1991). That evidence is dyadic. In the egalitarian face Reciprocity is her felt reading of what the group as a whole returns to her, so the step to the circle closing round her is an extension. Help that comes back also produces positive feeling attached to the group (Lawler 2001, affect theory of social exchange), and gratitude binds the one helped closer to the helper (Algoe 2012); those raise her own warmth, which belongs to E:Engagement->Belonging, so they do not drive this card. Her Belonging moves with how they treat her when she comes back.

Pre-language (increment): When what she shares comes back and she is fed and groomed in need, she is drawn closer to the others and they to her: her feeling of being welcome among them rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When she gives and nothing comes back, and she is passed over in need, she drifts to the edge of their company: her feeling of being welcome among them falls.

Here to Help: Reciprocity to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When what I put in comes back from the group, a clash with one of them does not leave me braced: we make it up soon, the fidgeting and watchfulness after it fade, and I go back to letting slips, moods and disagreements show: my felt safety to show myself rises.

Decrement: When what I give goes into a hole, I have no ties here worth mending, so a clash is left unmended; I stay on edge around the one I clashed with, fidget and mask my moods and disagreements, braced for a put-down: my felt safety to show myself falls.

After aggression, primate victims show more self-scratching and self-grooming and run a higher risk of renewed attack, and friendly reunions reduce both (Aureli and van Schaik 1991). Reunions happen most where the relationship is valuable (Cords and Thurnheer 1993; Aureli, Cords and van Schaik 2002). That evidence is dyadic. In the egalitarian face the return comes from the group, so a member who feels help comes back counts her ties with any member as worth repairing; that step is an extension. Conflict then leaves her less braced to show herself.
