The primate anxiety concerns renewed attack; the card takes only its milder human counterpart, being braced for a put-down, since fear of force is Parity's ground (E:Reciprocity->Levelling). The same mend also moves Belonging (E:Reciprocity->Belonging), which feeds Safety (E:Belonging->DivsExp), so play this card small.

Pre-language (increment): When the band meets her need and gives back what she shared, she feels safe among them, and lets her slips, moods and wants show without bracing for a slap-down.

Pre-language (decrement): When her need goes unmet and nothing she shared comes back, she feels unprotected, masks her moods and hides even a plain want, braced to be snapped at or turned from.

Mucking in Together: Reciprocity to GrpProsp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When what I put in comes back and whoever needs help gets it, I feel the group covers its own weak spots, and my confidence that it can pull off the venture we have set ourselves rises.

Decrement: When what I give goes into a hole and need goes unmet while others could see it, I feel those who struggle will be left to fall short, and my confidence that the group can pull off the venture falls.

Where help flows to whoever needs it, members' gaps are covered by others, so the group can do more than its weakest hands alone; she reads that in the help she sees given and returned. Where need goes unmet in plain view, she expects the weak spots to stay open. Backup is a core teamwork process (Marks, Mathieu and Zaccaro 2001; Porter et al. 2003), and helping goes with the quantity and quality of work-group output (Podsakoff, Ahearne and MacKenzie 1997). Backing up also has costs, since helpers can neglect their own tasks and those helped can ease off later (Barnes et al. 2008), so keep the rise moderate. The step from help seen to her felt confidence in the venture is common sense.

Pre-language (increment): When the band shares food and help with whoever falls short, she feels them strong together, and goes to the shared hunt sure of the kill.

Pre-language (decrement): When those who have hide it and the weak are left to struggle, she feels the band falling short, and goes to the shared hunt expecting it to fail.

Helpers stand together: Reciprocity to Levelling (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When what I give comes back from the group as a matter of course, I count on help coming back too if anyone tries to set themselves over me, and I go about my business beside the strongest as freely as beside anyone: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me rises.

Decrement: When nothing I give comes back from the group, I cannot count on anyone's help if the strongest turns on me, and I start to watch him warily and give way: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me falls.

Help repaid includes help in a quarrel. Among primates, grooming is exchanged for support in conflicts, though the pooled effect is small (Schino 2007, meta-analysis), and chimpanzee males gain alpha status through coalitional backing (de Waal 1982, Chimpanzee Politics). Those trades run between particular partners. Among egalitarian peoples, subordinates acting together keep a would-be dominant in check (Boehm 1993). The step from help coming back from the group to counting on the group's backing against a would-be dominant is the model's own and rests on common sense: people who repay favours as a matter of course can be expected to repay them in a quarrel too. Play it moderately. Where her help comes back from the group, she counts on its backing against anyone who would set himself over her, and the fear goes out of a strong member's presence; where it does not, she stands alone. The card rests on the return she can count on, not on being wanted (E:Belonging->Levelling) or on her own commitment (E:Engagement->Levelling).

Pre-language (increment): When the others share back with her and console her freely, she feels them as allies and feeds and moves near the strongest without a glance at their mood: her sense that no one can make her yield rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When nothing passes back to her from the others, she feels unbacked, goes still when a strong one approaches and gives up her place to them: her sense that no one can make her yield falls.

Good for Their Word: Reciprocity to OutResp (Reinforce, E)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When what I put in comes back from the group as a matter of course, I feel these are people who look out for more than themselves, and I leave their part of the shared work in their hands without checking and give a slip the benefit of the doubt: my sense that they can be counted on rises.

Decrement: When what I give goes into a hole and my needs go unmet, I feel these people look after themselves first, and I start checking up on their part of the shared work, expecting them to shirk it: my sense that they can be counted on falls.

The card assumes, on common sense, that trust built in one exchange carries over to other dealings with the same people. When an employer fails to deliver what it promised in exchange, employees' trust falls and their contributions fall with it, and trust, together with unmet expectations, carries that effect (Robinson 1996); across studies, breach is followed by mistrust and a sense of violation, which carry its effects onto work attitudes (Zhao et al. 2007). Those studies concern the employer, not fellow members, so the carry-over to members' carrying of their parts is an extension; keep it moderate. Prior trust also softens the reading of later breaches (Robinson 1996), which the increment carries: a member whose help comes back gives others' lapses the benefit of the doubt.

Pre-language (increment): When the band gives back what she has shared, she leaves the shared task in their hands and stops looking over at it.

Pre-language (decrement): When nothing comes back from those she shared with, she eyes them at the shared task, watching for them to slack, and does their bit over herself.

Clinging or letting go: Belonging to NormExp (Discretionary, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Felt inclusion sets her stake in the settled order, and the direction depends on what her place rests on. Circumstance one, her place is still on trial (a newer choir member whose place rests on being seen to keep the ways). HIGH: kept securely among them, she has nothing to prove and lets small departures pass, so her Rule-Keeping falls. LOW: feeling herself edged out, she is jarred by every departure from the settled ways and pulls others up on it sharply, so her Rule-Keeping rises (here the card runs as Inverse). Evidence: peripheral members of a valued group are harsher towards outsiders when other members can see, while core members do not change with audience (Noel, Wann and Branscombe 1995). That concerns public negativity towards outgroups, not indignation at an ingroup breach, and its dependence on an audience suggests display as much as felt indignation; so the step to circumstance one is a proposal, and the felt rise should be played modestly, larger when other members are watching. Circumstance two, the ways have long been her own (a long-standing club member). HIGH: kept among them, she feels a breach of the club's ways as a breach of her own and pulls the breacher up, so her Rule-Keeping rises. LOW: pushed aside for good, she is no longer stung when others break ways that have stopped being hers, and lets it pass, so her Rule-Keeping falls (here the card runs as Reinforce). Circumstance two rests on the black sheep effect, harsher judgement of an ingroup member who lets the group down (Marques, Yzerbyt and Leyens 1988), found stronger among highly identified members, at least when the group's identity is under threat (Branscombe, Wann, Noel and Coleman 1993). Felt acceptance is not identification; the circumstance supplies the identification, and Belonging only keeps it alive. Identification itself already moves Rule-Keeping through H:Engagement->NormExp, so play circumstance two's rise small, for the acceptance alone. The withdrawal branch of circumstance two is own proposal, in keeping with chronic exclusion leading to resignation and withdrawal (Williams 2007). Default: circumstance one in a member's first months, circumstance two after.

Pre-language (explanation): While her place is still new, slipping toward the edge sets her bristling at any new way and she snaps at whoever tries it, while being held close lets her settle and let it pass. Once the ways are long her own, being held close leaves her bristling at anyone who breaks them, while being left right out means others' new ways no longer stir her and she lets them pass.

Kept close, near the food: Belonging to OwnProsp (Reinforce, H)

Generated for the draft model; provisional, awaiting Ben Rechecked 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars: kept.

Increment: When I am kept among them in my place, I feel within reach of the shares, mates and chances the group holds, and my sense that staying will get me what I am after rises.

Decrement: When I am kept at the edge, I feel far from what the group holds while those kept close get it, and my sense that staying will get me what I am after falls.

In a ranked group, being kept close is access: to shares, partners and allies. Among primates, grooming is traded for tolerance at food (de Waal 1997, the chimpanzee's service economy), females compete to groom those of high rank for their support (Seyfarth 1977, a model of grooming among female monkeys), and in despotic species rank shapes access to resources and support (Sapolsky 2005). Those findings concern rank and favours traded with a partner. The step to felt inclusion as access in its own right, and from food to the shares, mates and chances of a human group, rests on common sense: what the group holds is handed out among those present and in favour. Nearness to the core goes largely with rank, so scale the move to the access that being kept close adds at her rank, not to the rank itself. The card reads access through being kept close, not through rank (H:Status->OwnProsp), and not through favours traded with a particular partner, such as grooming repaid with tolerance at food, which belong to H:Reciprocity->OwnProsp.

Pre-language (increment): When she is let near and kept in the troop's company, she feeds and seeks partners with energy, and her hope of getting what she is after rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is pushed to the edge, she hangs back from food and partners, and her hope of getting what she is after sinks.

Out of Sight, Not Copied: Belonging to Prestige (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When I am kept among them in my place, I feel what I bring is in their sight, and as they watch how I do it and bring me their problems, my sense that they turn to me for it rises.

Decrement: When I am kept at the edge, I feel what I bring is out of their sight, and I see them turn to someone nearer when my kind of skill is needed: my sense that they turn to me for it falls.

Deference for skill needs the skill to be in view. Coussi-Korbel and Fragaszy (1995) propose, in a model built on nonhuman animals, that social spacing and coordination shape who learns from whom; it is a framework with predictions, not a test. The rest rests on common sense: in a ranked group a member kept in the company is watched and looked to, while one kept at the edge is copied less, whatever her skill, and being watched for a skill leads others to turn to her for it. Nearness only puts what she brings in view: scale the rise to what she brings the group, and set it near nil where she brings little it values.

Pre-language (increment): When she is kept in the troop's company, the young sit near and watch her crack nuts, and her feeling of being looked to rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is kept at the edge, the young crowd round others at the nut stones, and her feeling of being looked to sinks.

Kept in, deals open: Belonging to Reciprocity (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When I am kept among them, the partners I help know I am there to call a favour in and that the others would see if they shorted me, and my sense that the partners I help will pay me back rises.

Decrement: When I am kept at the edge, I am not there to call a favour in and no one would mind if a partner shorted me, so I expect partners to take and not return: my sense that anyone I help will pay me back falls.

Exchange with a particular partner holds while defaulting would cost the partner: reciprocal cooperation is stable when future dealings are expected (Axelrod 1984). Inclusion keeps her on hand to call the favour in, and among others who would see a partner short her. People give more to those seen to give (Wedekind and Milinski 2000, replicated in part by Russell, Stoilova and Dosoftei 2020), so a partner's standing with those others rides on how they treat her. That onlookers care less when a partner shorts a member kept at the edge is the model's own step, resting on common sense. Exclusion takes both away, so a partner can short the one at the edge, who is neither there to hold them to it nor watched over by anyone who would. The felt horizon of her own staying belongs to H:Engagement->Reciprocity; this card reads only the others' inclusion of her.

Pre-language (increment): When she is kept close in the troop, those she grooms groom her back and those she backs back her, and she settles into the give-and-take expecting return.

Pre-language (decrement): When she is pushed to the edge, those she grooms move off without returning it, and she stops expecting anything back from them.

Kept close while I keep my place: Engagement to Belonging (Reinforce, H)

Engagement card, generated for the draft model; provisional, awaiting Ben Rechecked 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars: kept.

Increment: When this group feels part of who I am, keeping to my place comes easily, and the slot they give me at each gathering reads as a real place among them; my sense that they want me among them rises.

Decrement: When I am pulling out of this group, the terms of my slot gall me and I hang at the margin, and I read that margin as where they have put me; my sense that they want me among them falls.

In ranked groups inclusion often comes on terms: one is kept close so long as one keeps one's place. The model offers this as common sense, with no checked source. A member who has invested more accepts the terms easily and reads her slot as a real place. A member who has withdrawn finds the terms galling, drifts outward, and then reads the periphery as where she has been put. People who expect rejection are quick to see it in others' behaviour (Downey and Feldman 1996, on a disposition in close relationships). The step from her own investment to that reading is a proposal on common sense. Sociometer theory (Leary and Baumeister 2000) supplies only the reading of inclusion from others' treatment; it does not run from investment to that reading.

Pre-language (increment): Settled in the troop, she yields readily and is let in close, and she takes the closeness as her place. Her feeling of being kept among them rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Restless in the troop, she yields grudgingly and lingers at its edge, and she feels herself pushed out. Her feeling of being kept among them falls.

Invested, I guard our ways: Engagement to NormExp (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When I have put much of myself into the group, another member's break from our settled ways strikes me as an affront to what is ours, and I judge it the more harshly; my sense that such a breach is plainly wrong rises.

Decrement: When I am holding back from the group, another member's departure from our settled ways barely touches me, and I let it pass; my sense that such a breach is wrong falls.

Fellow members who break the group's norms are judged more harshly than outsiders who do the same (the black sheep effect: Marques, Yzerbyt and Leyens 1988). Highly identified members judge a disloyal fellow member more harshly still, at least when the group's identity is under threat (Branscombe, Wann, Noel and Coleman 1993). High identifiers have also been found to act more in line with the ingroup's norm than low identifiers, whether that norm favours the ingroup or fairness (Jetten, Spears and Manstead 1997); her own conformity is not Rule-Keeping, so this is context only. On common sense, as investment rises the settled ways feel more like her own, and a breach by another feels like damage to something of hers. Packer's normative conflict model (Packer 2008) adds a boundary: strongly identified members may dissent when they judge a norm harmful, but that is a reflective act outside this model. Packer also separates nonconformity from disengagement from dissent. That a disengaged member has no stake in the ways, so a breach leaves her unmoved and Rule-Keeping falls, rests on common sense.

Pre-language (increment): Having just thrown herself in, she bristles when another starts doing things a new way, and threatens or turns her back on them. Her indignation at the breach rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Having just drawn back, she watches another try a new way and feels nothing stir; she lets it pass. Her indignation at the breach falls.

Putting in, in line for my due: Engagement to OwnProsp (Discretionary, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Redrawn as Discretionary. Whether putting much of myself in raises or lowers my sense that staying will bring me what I am after depends on whether the group's dealings with me keep pace with what I put in. Circumstance one (the default), returns keep pace or are still unclear: places, shares and chances have come my way roughly in step with my effort, or nothing yet shows otherwise. HIGH: having put much in, I feel I have earned my due, and the group's dealings with me read as the way to what I came for opening up: my Payoff rises. LOW: having held back, I feel I have given them no reason to bring me on, and the way reads as closing: my Payoff falls. Circumstance two, returns are plainly flat: I have put in more and more while places, shares and chances go elsewhere. HIGH: the more I have put in, the more the flat return reads as being taken for granted, and I feel short-changed: my Payoff falls. LOW: having put in little, a flat return is no more than I looked for; the card adds nothing, and the scene alone moves my Payoff. Circumstance one is a proposal on common sense: a member's felt claim from what she has put in colours an ambiguous forecast. Circumstance two rests on equity theory: people weigh what they get against what they put in, and under-reward relative to input brings distress and anger (Adams 1965); in social exchange, giving creates an expectation of return (Blau 1964). Groups do repay contribution with status and influence (Willer 2009), but that route runs through H:Engagement->Status and H:Engagement->Prestige and on to Payoff, so this card carries only her felt claim; keep both circumstances modest. The card moves her forecast of what the group will deliver, and leaves her confidence in her own ability alone.

Pre-language (increment): Her investment has just deepened; she feels herself in line for the troop's favour and looks to it to bring her what she wants. Her hope of getting what she is after rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Her investment has just slackened; she feels herself out of favour and expects the troop to give her nothing. Her hope of getting what she is after falls.

Putting in, looked to: Engagement to Prestige (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When I am putting much of myself into the group, what I bring to each scene seems to show: I feel the others turning to me, watching how I do it and taking my advice, and my sense that they defer to me for what I bring rises.

Decrement: When I am putting little of myself into the group, I bring little to each scene, and I feel the others look past me to someone else when it counts; my sense that they defer to me for what I bring falls.

Esteem, in this model, is deference freely given to those whose skill or contribution others value. Members who contribute more to the group are given more status and influence (Willer 2009); treating that as Esteem is the model's mapping. That study rewards contribution as sacrifice; here only the deference for what she brings moves, and the others' verdict on whether she carries her share is Repute's (H:Engagement->Face carries the open charge). The reading is an inference from ambiguous cues, and on common sense her own recent conduct colours it: having just put in more, she reads others' questions and glances as turning to her; having just pulled back, she reads their turning elsewhere as her contribution no longer counting. People track how useful others find them as one part of their relational value (Leary 2005), so such a reading is one she is primed to make. Moderate confidence.

Pre-language (increment): Having just thrown herself into the work, she finds the others watching her, copying her and bringing her their troubles. Her sense of being looked to rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Having just drawn back, she sees the others pass her by and turn to another when the work needs doing. Her sense of being looked to falls.

The long shadow of staying: Engagement to Reciprocity (Reinforce, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When I am putting much of myself into the group and mean to stay, I feel we will be around each other long enough for every favour to come back, and I read what I give my partners as sure to be repaid; my sense that help I give comes back from those I help rises.

Decrement: When I am putting little of myself into the group and am half out of the door, I feel I may not be around when a favour falls due, and I read my partners as having no reason to repay one who is leaving; my sense that help I give comes back from those I help falls.

Conditional exchange holds only while partners expect to meet again: the shadow of the future (Axelrod 1984). In lab games with anonymous pairs, cooperation is higher when play may continue than when the end is known, close to what theory predicts (Dal Bó 2005). How long she means to stay is part of Engagement: a member who has put much of herself in sees herself staying, one who is gone or going does not. High Engagement lengthens the felt horizon on both sides, so she reads her partners as bound to repay one who stays; on common sense the same holds for a patron across rank. Low Engagement shortens it, and she reads herself as the one partners will stop repaying. The partner face applies: what moves is her reading of the return, not her readiness to deal.

Pre-language (increment): Settled in the troop, she grooms her partners and feels them groom her back and come to her side in a fight. Her sense that her partners repay her rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Half gone from the troop, she feels her partners slow to groom her back or to come to her aid. Her sense that her partners repay her falls.

Staying put, given way to: Engagement to Status (Reinforce, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (second round); provisional

Increment: When this group is part of who I am, I am there at every turn and share and stand on my place; when someone above me hangs back or is away, I step into the turn they leave and the others let me: my felt rung in the order rises.

Decrement: When I am pulling out of this group, I no longer stand on my place; I hang back and let others take the first turn and the first share, and they go before me as if I were already gone: my felt rung in the order falls.

A proposal on common sense: precedence here is owed to place, and a place is held by one who stays in it. Members above and below are always drifting, falling away or leaving, and the turns and shares they stop standing on pass to whoever is there to step into them. A member for whom the group is part of who she is is always there, steps into the precedence others leave, and is let keep it, so over many plays she moves up the order as far as kin, allies and office allow. One who is withdrawing stops standing on her place, hangs back, and is passed over as if already gone, which she feels as her rung slipping. Seniority in human organisations works the same way; animal cases of rank passing by queue or tenure (Kokko and Johnstone 1999; East and Hofer 2001) await checking. Standing won by contribution routes through H:Prestige->Status; this card covers only holding and taking up place by staying.

Pre-language (increment): Always about the troop, she moves up to the food when one above her hangs back or is gone, and the others let her go before them from then on: her felt place in the order rises.

Pre-language (decrement): Drifting from the troop, she hangs back and others go to the food before her: her felt place in the order falls.

Guarding the ways earns a place: NormExp to Belonging (Discretionary, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Whether pulling up a breach draws the others round her depends on whether they share the bristle. Circumstance one, the others share the bristle: the breach falls short of what the group plainly stands for, or overshoots it in a way they resent, and they are already muttering (a member skipping the rota the rest keep). HIGH: she pulls the breacher up, the others close ranks with her, and her Belonging rises. LOW: she lets it pass while they bristle, they read her as soft on the ways and cool towards her, and her Belonging falls. Circumstance two, the others do not share the bristle (a small departure the settled ways frown on but the rest would shrug off). HIGH: she pulls up a member the others think harmless; they read her as a scold setting herself above them and edge away, so her Belonging falls. LOW: she lets it pass with the rest and stays one of them, so her Belonging holds or rises a little. In either circumstance, where HIGH has her pulling up a member well above her own place, the act reads as stepping out of line and her Belonging falls; what it does to her rung belongs to H:NormExp->Status. Members derogate fellow members who depart from the group's norm in a direction it condemns (Abrams et al. 2000); that a member who sides with the group against such a breach is drawn closer is the model's step, resting on common sense. Groups can also sanction those who contribute more than the norm (Herrmann, Thoni and Gachter 2008), so judge an overshoot by the others' reaction. People also put down the morally motivated who seem to reproach them (Minson and Monin 2012); that study measured disparagement of an out-group minority, so the step to fellow members edging away from a scold within the group rests on common sense. Third-party punishers are trusted (Jordan et al. 2016), but trust is not inclusion. Circumstance one is the default in ranked groups with settled ways.

Pre-language (increment): When she bristles and threatens a member trying a new way, others side with her and keep her close, and her sense of being kept in the troop rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When she lets a member's new way go unchallenged, others turn from her, and her sense of being kept in the troop sinks.

Loyalty repaid: NormExp to Reciprocity (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When another member's breach jars me and I pull them up, the partners I deal with see that I hold to our ways and can be relied on, and those above me see loyalty they owe favour for: my sense that the partners I help will pay me back rises.

Decrement: When a breach leaves me unmoved and I let it pass while my partners look on, they see no sign that I can be relied on, and those above me see no loyalty to repay: my sense that the partners I help will pay me back falls.

Third-party punishers are trusted more, and in fact behave more trustworthily, than non-punishers (Jordan, Hoffman, Bloom and Rand 2016); punishment works as a signal that the punisher can be relied on. That evidence concerns punishing unfair splits in economic games; the step to pulling up a breach of the group's settled ways rests on common sense. That the trust brings back what she gives is an inference: partners choose and keep up exchanges with those they judge reliable, so her help to them is more readily returned. Across rank, holding the line on the group's ways reads as loyalty passed up, which a patron repays with favour and protection; this step rests on common sense. Where she pulls up a member above her own place, those above read it as stepping out of line rather than loyalty; that route belongs to H:NormExp->Status, so set the rise near nil there. Both lines also need a breach the others bristle at too: where they think it harmless, pulling up reads as scolding and letting it pass as ordinary (H:NormExp->Belonging, circumstance two), so set both moves near nil. With the Reputation expansion pack in play, the open standing she wins as one who holds the line runs through H:NormExp->Face and H:Face->Reciprocity; this card then carries only the reliance her partners take from what they saw themselves, and should be smaller still. The signal weakens where she can show her worth by helping directly, and the decrement needs her partners to have seen her let the breach pass, so the card should be modest.

Pre-language (increment): When she threatens a member trying a new way, the higher-ranked one she sided with backs her in her next squabble and lets her share its food.

Pre-language (decrement): When she lets a member's new way go by, the higher-ranked ones do not come to her side when she is threatened.

Pulling up within or beyond place: NormExp to Status (Discretionary, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (second round); provisional

Whether a member's indignation at a breach moves her precedence depends on whose breaches come before her. Circumstance one, members ranked below her are breaking the settled ways, pressing in at turns and shares. HIGH: pulling up a junior is what her place allows; the others back her, the juniors who had begun crowding in are put back behind her, and she takes again the first turns they had been taking from her, so her Rank rises. LOW: letting juniors' breaches pass lets them edge ahead of her at turns and shares, so her Rank falls. Circumstance two, a member ranked above her breaks the settled ways and others at her rung pull that senior up. HIGH: she joins in, oversteps her place with them, and is put back and made to wait her turn, so her Rank falls. LOW: the senior's breach leaves her unmoved and she lets it pass, which is what her place calls for; those of her rung who objected are put back, and she now goes before them at turns and shares, so her Rank rises. Evidence: circumstance two extends a checked finding, since members who claim more standing than the group grants them are liked less and paid less (Anderson, Ames and Gosling 2008); the step from that to a junior pulling up a senior is a proposal. Punishing a norm breaker can also win the punisher trust (Jordan et al. 2016), so set the circumstance-two fall small. Where the whole group turns on the senior, no objector is put back and joining in oversteps nothing, so set both circumstance-two moves near nil. Circumstance one is a proposal: rank carries the licence to correct those below, common sense in any ranked group.

Pre-language (explanation): Whether her bristling at a new way shifts her place depends on who it came from. When lower-ranked members start pushing in at the food, snapping at them sends them back and she eats before them again, while letting them be sees them push ahead of her. When a higher-ranked one does something new and others of her standing snap at it, snapping with them gets her threatened back and made to wait until the others have eaten, while keeping still sees those who snapped pushed back and her going to the food before them.

Reaching within or beyond place: OwnProsp to Belonging (Discretionary, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Whether the ranked group keeps her close depends on whether her aims lie within what her rank allows. Circumstance one, aims within her place. HIGH: a junior in a club, hopeful of mastering a skill the seniors are glad to pass on, stays close, eager and deferential, and is kept among them, so her Belonging rises. LOW: seeing nothing here for her, she hangs back when the seniors gather and does not seek them out, and no one draws her in, so her Belonging falls. Circumstance two, aims beyond her place. HIGH: hopeful of a role a senior holds, she starts reaching for it, is cold-shouldered and edged out, so her Belonging falls. LOW: having given up on the senior's role, she stops reaching and gives the seniors no cause to edge her out, so her Belonging holds or rises a little. Circumstance two extends a checked finding: members who overrate their standing in the group are liked less (Anderson, Ames and Gosling 2008). That study measured self-perceived status and liking, so the step to a member reaching for a senior's role and being edged out rests on common sense; keep the circumstance-two fall moderate. Circumstance one is own proposal resting on common sense.

Pre-language (explanation): Hope draws her in close to pursue her aim. If what she reaches for is hers to take at her rank, she is let stay close and her place among them firms, and when hope fails she drifts off and is left at the edge. If she reaches for what a higher-ranked member holds, she is threatened and pushed to the edge, and when she gives it up and keeps to her place she is let back among them.

Valued service, kept place: Prestige to Belonging (Reinforce, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When the others turn to me for what I bring, watch how I do it and take my advice, I feel them keep me near because they need me, the threat of being dropped seems far off, and my sense of being kept among them rises.

Decrement: When no one asks me or copies me and they turn to someone else when my kind of skill is needed, I feel that nothing I bring holds me in and that one step out of line would see me dropped, and my sense of being kept among them falls.

Groups repay valued contributors with freely conferred deference (Henrich and Gil-White 2001), and followers are held to repay a leader's valued service with prestige (Price and Van Vugt 2014, a theory review). That followers also keep close to those they learn from rests on common sense here, since the checked reading of Henrich and Gil-White did not confirm it. Under this deck's face, being kept among them rests on keeping her place, and she reads it partly from the standing threat of being dropped. A member the others turn to feels that threat recede, because the group needs what she brings; one passed over feels nothing she brings holds her in, so her keeping feels more conditional. These two steps rest on common sense. The card moves her felt security of being kept, not her place.

Pre-language (increment): When others watch her work and copy her, they sit close by her and no one moves to push her out, and her sense of being kept in the troop rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When others stop watching her and go to another to learn, they sit by that one instead and she feels easily pushed out, and her sense of being kept in the troop sinks.

Comfortable in my Own Skin: Prestige to NormExp (Inverse, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When no one turns to me, watches or copies me any more, my footing feels hollow, and another member's break from the settled ways jars me as wrong: I bristle and pull them up, and my sense that such a breach is plainly wrong rises.

Decrement: When the others turn to me, copy how I do things and bring me their problems, my footing feels earned, and another member's break from the settled ways jars me less: I am readier to let it pass, and my sense that such a breach is wrong falls.

The mechanism is threat. Feeling that no one defers to her for what she brings is a threat to her worth in the group; that step rests on common sense. Self-uncertainty draws people to groups with clear normative prescriptions (Hogg 2014). When a person who holds power feels her competence is in doubt, she turns on others in hostile ways, and affirming her self-worth removes the effect (Fast and Chen 2009). That study concerns aggression towards others in general, not indignation at a breach of the group's ways, so carrying it to Rule-Keeping is an extension; keep the effect moderate. The settled ways are ground on which her place is still secure, so another member's breach jars as a further threat and strikes her as wrong: Rule-Keeping rises. When others defer to her for what she brings, the threat lifts and a breach jars less: Rule-Keeping falls. The evidence shows the threat adding hostility and affirmation taking that addition away, so the fall should be smaller than the rise. The card follows a single source level. Her own conformity and her openness to new ideas are not Rule-Keeping and are left to other Pillars' cards. Fast and Chen's finding concerns power-holders whose competence is in doubt, so the effect is strongest where Rank is high and Esteem low, and modest otherwise.

Pre-language (increment): When others stop watching and copying her and take their troubles to another, she grows tense and keeps to the troop's familiar routines, threatening or turning from any member who starts a new way; her guarding of the settled ways rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When others watch and copy her and bring their troubles to her, she is loose and unthreatened, and lets a member who starts a new way go on unchallenged; her guarding of the settled ways eases.

Looked To, Let In: Prestige to OwnProsp (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When the others turn to me for what I bring, take my advice and hand me jobs that matter, I feel doors opening for me here, and my sense that staying will bring me what I came for rises.

Decrement: When no one asks me or copies me and they turn to someone else, and the jobs that matter go elsewhere, I feel the way to what I came for closing, and my sense that staying will bring it falls.

Under this deck's face, being deferred to includes being handed decisions and jobs that matter, and these open the way to the place, skill or advancement a member came for, so felt deference carries a forecast of what the group will deliver to her. Henrich and Gil-White (2001) hold that the prestigious receive freely conferred benefits from those who defer to them; the step from those benefits to her forecast of what staying will bring rests on common sense. Whether help she gives comes back is Reciprocity's ground (H:Prestige->Reciprocity), so this card carries only the opening of the way to what she came for.

Pre-language (increment): When the others watch and copy her, she feels the troop's food and partners within her reach, and her hope of getting what she is after rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When they turn to another to watch and copy, she feels shut out of what the troop holds, and her hope of getting what she is after sinks.

Sought-After Partner: Prestige to Reciprocity (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: When the others turn to me for what I bring, I feel my help is worth a good deal to them, and my sense that the partners I help will pay me back rises.

Decrement: When no one asks me or copies me any more, I feel my help is worth little to them, and my sense that partners will repay what I give falls.

In a market for partners, exchange rates follow supply and demand, so a partner in demand can command better terms (Noe and Hammerstein 1994, modelled in non-human animals; applying it to a member valued for her skill is the model's extension). As deference fades, so does what partners will give back.

Pre-language (increment): When the others watch and copy her, those she grooms groom her back at length, and she feels sure of return.

Pre-language (decrement): When the others turn to another to watch and copy, those she grooms move off without returning it, and she stops expecting return.

Trading partners keep you close: Reciprocity to Belonging (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When my partners pay me back and those I ask deliver, we are worth too much to each other to lose: they let me sit close, and after a clash with one of them I go to them soon, low and friendly, and am let close again. I am kept among them in my place, and my sense of being kept among them rises.

Decrement: When partners take and do not return and what I ask for goes unmet, no one makes room for me beside them, and a clash with one of them is left unmended; I keep out of their way, no one draws me back, and I am left at the margin: my sense of being kept among them falls.

In ranked groups grooming and favours are exchanged for tolerance and support, a prediction that tests have mostly but not uniformly confirmed (Seyfarth 1977); grooming is reciprocated across primate groups (Schino and Aureli 2008), and partner value predicts reconciliation after conflict (Aureli, Cords and van Schaik 2002; Cords and Thurnheer 1993). A partner who repays is a valuable partner: she is tolerated close day to day, and repair with her after a clash keeps a member in the troop's company. An unrepaired rift with a partner who never repaid leaves her at the edge. Reconciliation repairs one partnership; reading it as being kept among the others as a whole is an extension, which holds best where her partners are the ones whose company makes up the group.

Pre-language (increment): When her grooming is returned and partners back her, they tolerate her close by, and her feeling of being kept close grows.

Pre-language (decrement): When partners take her grooming and give none back, they drift from her, and her feeling of being kept close fades.

Power to your Elbow: Reciprocity to OwnProsp (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: When the partners I help pay me back and those I ask deliver, I feel backed, and what I came for feels within reach here.

Decrement: When partners take and do not return and those I ask do not deliver, I feel on my own, and what I came for slips further away.

Proposal on common sense, pending a check of Schino 2007 (grooming and agonistic support): in ranked groups, partners who repay favours may also back a member and tolerate her near resources (predicted by Seyfarth 1977, with mixed tests). Read in a human group, a member whose partners pay her back feels backed and expects staying to open the way to what she came for; one whose help is not returned stands alone and expects little from the group.

Pre-language (increment): Helped when she reaches for it, she feels backed and goes for what she wants here as one sure of getting it.

Pre-language (decrement): Left unhelped when she needs it, she feels alone and hangs back, as if what she wants here is out of reach.

Rank draws the circle: Status to Belonging (Reinforce, H)

Fixed 3 Nov 2026 after the final high and low check (fixed); provisional

Increment: When I go first as a matter of course and take the first share and the best seat, the others cluster round me and I feel no threat of being dropped: my sense of being kept among them in my place rises.

Decrement: When I go last and take what is left, I feel how little slack my place gives me and that any step out of line would see me dropped: my sense of being kept among them falls a little.

In ranked groups grooming tends to be directed up the order (Seyfarth 1977; tests mixed). Higher status is also accorded respect and voluntary deference (Anderson, Hildreth and Howland 2015), though their status includes deference freely given, which is Esteem's ground here, so it supports this card only loosely. Under this deck's face a place is made for members high or low who keep to it, so rank does not decide inclusion outright; what moves is the felt threat of being dropped. A member who goes first feels her keeping is beyond question; one who goes last feels how little slack her place gives her, and that any step out of line would see her dropped. Status shielded its holders from punishment for low-severity deviance but became a liability for high-severity deviance (Karelaia and Keck 2013), so the slack a high rung gives covers small lapses, not serious ones. That work concerns formal leaders and observers' punishment; carrying it to the felt security of being kept among peers is a proposal. A member settled at the bottom who keeps to her place may still feel fairly secure, so the fall there is modest. Anxiety about exclusion among middle-status members (Phillips and Zuckerman 2001) cannot be carried by a card that follows a single source level and is left to play.

Pre-language (increment): When others yield her the first turn, they groom her and cluster near her, and her feeling of being kept close grows.

Pre-language (decrement): When she goes last to everything, others groom her less and she feels how easily she could be left at the edge, and her feeling of being kept close fades.

Self Interest Quo: Status to NormExp (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: Secure at the top of the order, I feel a member's break from the settled ways as a break in the order that puts me first; it jars at once and I pull them up: my sense that such a breach is plainly wrong rises.

Decrement: Low in the order, the settled ways are what keep me last, so a member breaking from them stirs less in me, though I still bristle a little, and I am slower to pull them up: my sense that such a breach is wrong falls a little.

Proposal, modest weight. Those an order puts first have most to lose by a breach of it, so a breach of the settled ways jars them as a breach of their own place; those it holds at the bottom have less stake. The indignation is felt, not reasoned. Social dominance theory concerns attitudes to rank between social groups and is a trait measure, so it is set aside. The nearest checked support is the black sheep effect: an unlikeable ingroup member is judged more harshly than a matching outgroup member (Marques, Yzerbyt and Leyens 1988). That study compared ingroup with outgroup and did not measure identification; the further claim that high identifiers judge ingroup deviants most harshly rests on later work not yet checked for this card (Branscombe et al. 1993; Castano et al. 2002). Nothing there links it to rank, and treating a high place as one ground of identification is the model's step, resting on common sense. Middle-status conformity (Phillips and Zuckerman 2001) concerns members' own conformity, and later work finds the pattern depends on ascribed status and reverses for actors of low ascribed status (Prato and colleagues 2019), so it bounds the slope only loosely. The earlier appeal to system justification is withdrawn: the claim that the disadvantaged legitimise the order more than others did not hold across three large representative data sets (Brandt 2013). Keep the decrement small for a different reason: a low-ranked member who identifies with the group still bristles at breaches by the black sheep route. The card follows a single source level and cannot carry a middle peak; H:Belonging->NormExp (Clinging or letting go) carries the insecure middle. Only her reaction to others' breaches moves here.

Pre-language (increment): Secure at the top, she bristles when another member does something in a new way, and threatens them or turns her back on them.

Pre-language (decrement): Low in the order, she watches another member do something in a new way and lets it pass, unbothered.

Built-in Advantage: Status to OwnProsp (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (reword); provisional

Increment: Going first as a matter of course, with the first turn and the first share mine without a word said, I feel the group opening the way to what I came for, and my sense that staying will bring it to me rises.

Decrement: Going last as a matter of course, waiting my turn and taking what is left, I feel what I came for slipping past me to those ahead, and my sense that staying will bring it to me falls.

Precedence is a standing claim on what the group hands out: the first turn, the first share and the best seat fall to the high-ranked before anyone else, so a member who goes first as a matter of course can expect what she came for to reach her, and one who goes last cannot. This rests on common sense about ordered access. Primate work on rank and priority of access to mates (Altmann 1962; Cowlishaw and Dunbar 1991) and on social queuing (Kokko and Johnstone 1999) points the same way, but none of it has been checked for this card and the card does not rely on it. Where the order is a queue by seniority, a low place is the start of the line and staying is how one moves up; play the decrement weak for a junior who expects to rise.

Pre-language (increment): High in the order, she takes first pick and others give way, and she goes after what she wants confident of getting it.

Pre-language (decrement): Low in the order, she waits on others' leavings, and expects to miss out on what she wants.

Repaid in order of rank: Status to Reciprocity (Reinforce, H)

Revised 3 Nov 2026 against the tightened Pillars (replace); provisional

Increment: Going first as a matter of course, I find that what I give comes back promptly and in full: those below answer my favours with service before anyone else's, and my sense that my partners pay me back rises.

Decrement: Going last as a matter of course, I find that the service I pass up comes back late and short: cover and favour from above reach me only after everyone above me has been served, and my sense that my partners pay me back falls.

Under this deck's face, those below repay those above with service, and what flows back down is mostly tolerance, cover and occasional support. The card's proposal, resting on common sense, is that precedence orders how soon and how fully returns come, as it orders shares, so the same exchange reads as well repaid from the top and thinly repaid from the bottom. Primate work on grooming running up the order and being exchanged in part for support (Seyfarth 1977; Schino 2001; Schino 2007) is consistent with this, but it has not been checked for this card and the card does not rely on it. The card moves her felt reading of returns from partners, not her readiness to help, and not whether others do their part of the shared work (Dependability).

Pre-language (increment): High in the order, she is groomed back at once and at length by those she grooms, and her sense that what she gives returns grows.

Pre-language (decrement): Low in the order, she grooms those above her and waits long for little in return, and her sense that what she gives returns fades.

Faltering venture tightens ranks: GrpProsp to NormExp (Inverse, H)

Increment: When I feel those at the top cannot steer us through what we have taken on, our settled ways look like all that still holds us on course, so a member doing things differently or pressing to change our ways jars me as wrong and I am quick to pull them up: my indignation at breaches rises.

Decrement: When I feel those at the top know the way through what we have taken on, a member trying something different or urging a change looks like no danger, since the course is in hands that will right it, and I let it pass: my indignation at breaches eases.

Deck H; the source is Team Confidence's hierarchical face. The nearest small-group evidence: in freely interacting groups an opinion deviate was rejected more when the dissent came close to the group's decision deadline, which the authors put down to a heightened need for collective closure (Kruglanski and Webster 1991). That study manipulated time pressure, not doubt about the venture; reading a faltering venture as raising the same need for closure is an inference. Across whole societies, histories of threat go with stronger norms and less tolerance of deviance (Gelfand et al. 2011), which points the same way but does not test a member's reaction to her group's venture. The face adds its own step, a proposal resting on common sense: in a ranked group the settled ways are partly the top's standing direction, so when live steering from the top looks weak, members lean harder on those ways and a departure reads as one more push off course; when steering looks sure, the top is trusted to catch a stray move, and it passes. Boundaries. The decrement covers departures that do not cross a call from the top; a member who defies the top's own direction is challenging the order, which this card does not carry, so keep the decrement small. Where the settled way is itself the top's failing course and the failure is openly acknowledged, departures can read as a needed correction; there the pull to guard the ways and the pull to welcome change offset each other, so the card does not fire and the step is nil. Both boundaries rest on common sense. The card covers the acute, felt jar of a venture slipping out of the leaders' grip, and the effect should be modest.

Pre-language (increment): When the band's venture is going badly and the prize looks out of reach, she clings to the usual way of doing it and bristles at a fellow who does it differently, with a protest or a shove. Her norm guarding rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When the prize looks well within the band's reach, she lets a fellow try an odd way of doing it without a second look. Her bristle at breaches subsides.

Shirkers sharpen the bristle: OutResp to NormExp (Inverse, X)

Increment: When I keep having to check up on, chase and redo what others took on, the next member who departs from the way we do the shared work jars me at once as plainly wrong, as if it were one more corner cut, and I pull them up with a sharp word or a turned back: my indignation at breaches rises.

Decrement: When I can leave any part of the work with any member, a member doing the shared work their own way strikes me as harmless, coming from people who deliver, and I let it pass: my indignation at breaches eases.

Negative emotions toward free riders appear to underlie costly punishment of them (Fehr and Gächter 2002; the emotion evidence is questionnaire-based), and unaffected observers also punish breaches of a cooperation norm, though less than those harmed (Fehr and Fischbacher 2004). The evidence concerns falling short on the cooperative task. The card's step, a proposal resting on common sense, is that where she has been left to chase and redo others' work, a member doing the shared work a different way is read as another dodge; the card is limited to the way the shared work is done. Where nearly everyone shirks, a departure stands out less against what the group actually does, and the threat of exclusion fails against a majority of shirkers (Kerr et al. 2009), so the increment is weak or nil there; it holds while she still reads doing one's part as the group's way. On the decrement side, conditional cooperators keep giving when others are seen to contribute (Fischbacher, Gächter and Fehr 2001); the step from there to letting a departure pass among people who deliver is a proposal resting on common sense. Idiosyncrasy credit, used here before as the brake, is dropped as support: direct tests are few and the leniency it implies is conditional. Keep the decrement smaller than the increment. The public goods evidence concerns contributions to a common pool and is shared with X:Reciprocity->NormExp; here it is read as doing one's part of the work, there as the ways of sharing, and each reading is the model's step.

Pre-language (increment): When the others keep leaving their end of the carry or the watch to her, she bristles sooner at any of them doing a thing the wrong way and moves to pull them up: a protest cry, a shove, a cold shoulder. Her norm guarding rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When the others reliably hold their end of the shared task, she meets a fellow's odd way of doing things with a shrug and goes about her business. Her bristle at breaches subsides.

Hoarders stir the levellers: Reciprocity to NormExp (Inverse, X)

provisional

Increment: When what I give the group stops coming back and what I need goes unmet, though sharing is still our way, a member stepping outside our settled ways of sharing and helping strikes me as wrong at once, and I am quick to mock or cold-shoulder them: my indignation at breaches rises.

Decrement: When whoever has gives to whoever needs and what I put in comes back from any member, a member who is slow to share or helps in a way of his own strikes me as no great matter, since it all comes back in the end, and I let it pass: my indignation at breaches eases.

When help stops coming back, a member's patience with those who step outside the ways of sharing and helping runs out. In a one-shot public goods experiment about half of subjects cooperated conditionally, giving more the more others gave (Fischbacher, Gächter and Fehr 2001). Negative emotions toward free riders appear to underlie costly punishment of them, even among strangers (Fehr and Gächter 2002; the emotion evidence is questionnaire-based). The increment rests on her own giving going unreturned. She is the cooperator who has been left short, and from that position the next departure from the ways of sharing jars at once. Where nobody shares any more, holding back is no departure from what the group actually does, and the increment is weak or nil; it holds while she still reads sharing as the group's settled way. This boundary rests on common sense. On the decrement side, a member secure in the return can afford to overlook an occasional lapse, which also rests on common sense. A flat refusal to share may still stand out the more in a high-giving group, so the decrement eases her reaction to small departures only; keep it smaller than the increment. The public goods evidence concerns contributions to a common pool and is shared with X:OutResp->NormExp; here it is read as the ways of sharing and helping, there as doing one's part of the work, and each reading is the model's step. Breaches in how the shared work is done belong to that card. The card reads her guarding of a settled way of sharing, which is Rule-Keeping's face; the levelling of a grabber who takes more than his due and makes it stick is Parity's ground and stays there, as Parity's definition draws it. The felt jar may run ahead of the voiced rebuke where her Rank or Parity is low.

Pre-language (increment): When her food goes out and nothing comes back while others hide their surplus, she bristles at fellows doing things the wrong way and moves to demand, protest or turn her back; her norm guarding rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When food passes freely and comes back to her from whoever next has, a fellow's odd way of doing things draws no bristle; her norm guarding falls.

Low in the order, guarded: Status to DivsExp (Reinforce, X)

provisional

Increment: When I hold a high place in this group's order, I expect an objection or a slip of mine to be let pass, with no one pouncing on it or turning away, so I let it show without softening it first: my felt safety to show myself rises.

Decrement: When I sit low in the order, I expect any objection or slip of mine to draw a put-down, so I soften every objection, swallow my first reaction and keep my slips out of sight: my felt safety to show myself falls.

A low place goes with expecting a put-down for any slip or objection, and a high place with expecting them to be let pass. Reduced power goes with attention to threat and inhibited social behaviour (Keltner, Gruenfeld and Anderson 2003); that is a theory paper about power, the control of resources and punishments, and carrying it to settled rank is the model's step. In hospital teams, higher profession-based status goes with greater psychological safety, and leader inclusiveness weakens the status gap (Nembhard and Edmondson 2006; checked against the abstract only). Embarrassment works as an appeasement display (Keltner and Buswell 1997), which fits the softening and hiding in the decrement line; tying it to rank is the model's step. Rank and safety stay distinct readings, since a member can be well placed in a group that punishes slips, or lowly in one that does not; an inclusive leader weakens the card. This card carries the route through settled place; E:Prestige->DivsExp carries the weaker route through live deference for what she brings. From the comparative psychologist's synthesis build (Standing->Safety), its most-used card.

Pre-language (increment): When she stands high in the band, she bares a protest openly and goes on, and no one turns on her for it. Her ease in showing herself rises.

Pre-language (decrement): When she stands low, she wraps any protest in appeasing grins and crouches, checks her first flare, and flushes and averts when caught out. Her ease in showing herself falls.

Heard from where I sit: Status to Prestige (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When I go first as a matter of course, the others take what I put forward to be good before it has shown its worth: they take up my suggestion, bring me the next problem and credit me with the result, and I feel them turn to me for what I bring: my sense that they defer to me for it rises.

Decrement: When I go last as a matter of course, what I put forward is passed over or credited to someone higher, however good it is, and I watch the next problem go to someone else: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring falls.

Status creates expectations that favour those already ahead, and status hierarchies reinforce themselves through those expectations (Magee and Galinsky 2008). Eminent people get more credit for comparable work (Merton 1968). Expectation states theory (Berger and colleagues) makes the same argument about who is listened to in task groups, but no primary source for it has been checked yet. Her rank colours the others' judgement of what she brings, and their deference follows that judgement, so the reading stays on Esteem's ground; deference owed to the place itself is Rank and is not carried here. The card moves her felt deference through the others' response to what she puts forward. With H:Prestige->Status it forms a reinforcing pair. The brake is Esteem evidence, a visible failure of what she brings. Proposal: the halo should be strongest when the worth of a contribution is hard to judge, since a plain result can be seen whoever offers it.

Settling into a place: Prestige to Status (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When the others keep turning to me for what I bring, hand me decisions and leave jobs that matter in my hands, they come to wait for me and give me the first word as a matter of course, and I feel it has become my place: my felt rung in the order rises.

Decrement: When what I bring stops counting and my word is doubted in front of the others, nothing that matters is handed to me, they stop waiting for me and someone else takes the first word, and I give way: my felt rung in the order slips a little.

Freely conferred deference is a route to rank (Henrich and Gil-White; Cheng et al.). Contributors are repaid with standing and influence (Willer), and perceived competence buys influence (Anderson and Kilduff). Once established, status holds itself through expectations (Magee and Galinsky). The step from live deference to a place taken for granted is slow. Proposal: each play moves Rank by a small fraction of Esteem's level, so the settling builds over many plays; make the decrement weaker than the increment, because a settled place outlasts the skill that earned it, as seniority and incumbency show every day. This card absorbs the older model's most-used card: being trusted with something that matters is Esteem evidence, and its settling is this card.

Backed into my place: Belonging to Status (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When I am kept among them and a place is made for me as a matter of course, a turn or a share of mine that someone questions is let stand by the room, the questioner gives way, and I take it without a word: my felt rung in the order, shaken by the question, firms up again.

Decrement: When I am kept at the edge and my turn or my share is questioned in front of the others, no one speaks for me, I give way, and others step ahead of me at turns and shares: my felt rung in the order falls.

In macaques, kin support matters for winning rank (Chapais and Larose 1988), though keeping rank among peers need not depend on it when subordinates cannot form coalitions (same source), and grooming is traded for agonistic support (Schino 2007), in line with Seyfarth's (1977) model of grooming directed up the hierarchy for rank-related benefits. Those findings concern support from particular partners in return for service. That is the ground of H Reciprocity, where a patron covers you. This card reads the acceptance of the group as a whole and takes from the primate work only that whether a challenge to a place succeeds depends partly on who backs it. The card therefore fires only when a turn or share of hers is contested, where backing decides who gives way; it does not carry a rank held steady by acceptance alone. The human step is a proposal, common sense in any committee: a member kept at the edge whose turn is questioned finds no one speaking for her and gives way, while one kept among them has her turn let stand. Hierarchical acceptance is held at any rung, high or low. The increment therefore only firms up a turn or share that was in doubt and never lifts her above her place; keep it smaller than the decrement. This carries the second half of the older model's most-used card. It is distinct from Esteem: the room's assent is for who she is to them, not for what she brings.

Friends get the rope: Belonging to OutResp (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When the others draw me in as one of their own, I hand them parts of the shared work without a second thought and leave them to it, and I see them carry it through: my confidence that they will do their part rises.

Decrement: When I am left at the edge, I keep the work in my own hands and check what little I hand over, so I see little of theirs carried through and nothing to set against the last let-down: my confidence that they will do their part falls.

Chimpanzees extend trust to friends more than to non-friends in a non-verbal trust game, though friends are no more trustworthy once trusted (Engelmann and Herrmann 2016). Trust games read whether what is entrusted comes back, which lies near Reciprocity; carrying the finding to confidence that members do their part of the work is by analogy. The felt shift at the cue is in how readily she trusts. The gain for Dependability builds across plays from sampling, a common-sense step pending a check of Fetchenhauer and Dunning 2010 and Denrell 2005: a member who trusts more sees more work carried through, while one who withholds trust sees little and has nothing to correct her last let-down. Control read as distrust lowers the other's effort (Falk and Kosfeld 2006), an effect that is real but usually small on replication (Ziegelmeyer, Schmelz and Ploner 2012), so over many plays withheld trust is partly self-fulfilling.

Generous, so sought: Reciprocity to Prestige (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When the partners I help pay me back as a matter of course, I give help freely, beyond any one partner and where the others can see it; they see what I bring, seek me out with their problems and take my advice, and I feel them turn to me: my sense that they defer to me for what I bring rises.

Decrement: When the partners I help do not pay me back, I stop giving beyond what I must; the others see less given by me and bring me fewer of their problems: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring falls a little.

In public settings, the most generous members gain the most status, here freely given deference (Esteem), and are the most preferred partners (Hardy and Van Vugt 2006), and contributors are given influence and deference (Willer 2009). Both studies concern contributions to a common pool; the step to help given beyond her own partners in the others' sight is by analogy. A felt return makes open-handed giving affordable to her, and the deference comes from the giving the others see, not from the return; giving the others read as a paid trade earns less of it. Each play moves her felt reading a step; the deference builds over many plays. Her name as a sharer is Repute's ground and is not carried here. The card carries the older build's Acceptance->Standing, with the giving now driven by felt return. It forms a positive loop with H:Prestige->Reciprocity; the brake is a partner who stops repaying.

Low rung, easy target: Status to Levelling (Reinforce, X)

provisional

Increment: When I hold a high place in a settled order, no one tries to push me about, take my due or pass me over when things are handed out, and I go about my business beside the strongest without a glance at their mood: my sense that no one here can force me, take more than their due or hand out unfairly, and get away with it, rises.

Decrement: When I sit low in the order, the one who likes to push finds me the easy target, taking more of my turns and my share than the order gives him, leaning on me, and passing me over when he hands things out to his own; I start to watch him and do what heads off his temper: my sense that no one here can force me, take more than their due or hand out unfairly, and get away with it, falls.

Rank shapes how much aggression and stress an animal receives, but direction and size depend on the society: subordination is most stressful in stable despotic orders and not in egalitarian ones, and in unstable orders the high-ranked face the most challenges (Sapolsky 2005); formalised, reconciled orders damp overt aggression (de Waal 1986). In a settled order she accepts, a low place moves Parity little, and an even-handed share-out that gives her less by rank leaves it high, as the Parity definition says; the card bites when someone uses her low place to push, take or pass her over. Set it small in settled orders and larger in despotic ones. While places are being contested, set the increment to zero, since a high place then draws challenges instead of shielding her.

Ideas aired, ideas taken up: DivsExp to Prestige (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When I feel safe to let a half-formed idea show, I put forward how we might do the work better in front of the others; they take it up and turn to me on it: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring rises.

Decrement: When I brace and keep my ideas masked, what I could bring stays in my head; the others never see it and turn to whoever spoke up instead: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring falls.

Felt psychological safety is taken as a precondition for letting half-formed ideas show, since an untested idea risks a slip or a disagreement shown, which is Safety's ground; the link from safety to voice is carried by Safety's evidence and is not rechecked here. Speaking up raises the status colleagues confer, partly because those who speak are seen as more agentic, and in two of three studies more communal (Weiss and Morrison 2019). Promotive voice, ideas for doing things better, raised peer-rated status and later leader emergence, while prohibitive voice, raising concerns, did not; men gained from promotive voice and women did not (McClean et al. 2018). Members high in trait dominance behave in ways that signal competence and are rated more competent by peers (Anderson and Kilduff 2009); that study is of dominance, so take it as light support that visible contribution earns a reputation for competence. The card covers ideas offered to improve the shared work; voicing alarm or criticism is not covered and may cost her. Where the group's norms follow McClean's pattern, set it smaller for women members; the gap rests on one set of field studies, so treat it as a caution. Deck E: the card reads Esteem's egalitarian face, deference freely given on the matter in hand with no right to command. It forms a Reinforce loop with E:Prestige->DivsExp; the brake is a visible failure of what she puts forward (Esteem evidence).

No passengers: OutResp to Levelling (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When every member carries through what they take on, the credit and reward each draws is earned by a part they have done, so no one gets more than our reckoning gives by coasting: my sense that no one here takes more than their due and keeps it holds or rises a little.

Decrement: When some members coast yet still draw the full share of credit and reward that our reckoning gives only to those who do their part, and no one makes them give it up, I see them taking more than their due and keeping it: my sense that no one here takes more than their due and keeps it falls.

In public goods games free riders draw an equal share of the pool while keeping their own stake, so they end ahead of those who contributed, and contributors' anger at them drives costly punishment (Fehr and Gächter 2002). The anger is Rule-Keeping's ground (X:OutResp->NormExp); the card takes from the study only that members read a coaster as ending ahead of what his part earns. Members also cut their own effort rather than carry a partner who free rides (the sucker effect: Kerr 1983), which does not move here. A coaster who draws the full share where the group's reckoning ties shares to doing one's part takes more than that reckoning gives, which is what Parity's second limb reads; the reading falls only when no one stops him and the grab sticks. The card holds only under such a reckoning. The game's own rule splits the pool equally, so players' tie of shares to contribution is inferred from the contributors' anger, not given by the game. Where the group's reckoning gives equal shares whatever each puts in, the coaster gets what the reckoning gives and Parity is untouched; where reward tracks each member's own output, shirking costs only the shirker. High reliability removes coasting as one route to an unearned share; it says nothing of grabbing or coercion by other means. Modest; forms a Reinforce loop with E:Levelling->OutResp.

Credit to spend: Prestige to DivsExp (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When the others turn to me for what I bring and take my advice, I feel a slip of mine would be put down to a bad day rather than held against me, and I let my doubts and disagreements show: my felt safety to show myself rises.

Decrement: When no one turns to me for anything I bring, I feel I have nothing to set against a slip, so I keep more of my doubts and disagreements masked: my felt safety to show myself falls a little.

Higher professional status goes with greater felt psychological safety (Nembhard and Edmondson 2006), and power releases approach and expression, while low power primes attention to threat and inhibition (Keltner, Gruenfeld and Anderson 2003). Both bear on settled place and power, which X:Status->DivsExp carries. The step to live deference is a proposal resting on common sense: a member the others turn to has something to set against a slip. Hollander's idiosyncrasy credit says members who have earned standing are allowed more latitude, but direct tests are few and weak, so it is not relied on. Deference that fades with what she brings is a thinner cushion than a settled place, so this card should be the weaker of the two.

Good season, open hands: GrpProsp to Reciprocity (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When the venture looks well within our reach, I am buoyed, I help whoever asks without counting, and the others do the same around me: my reading that help here comes back rises.

Decrement: When the venture looks beyond us, everyone hunches over their own part, help asked for is slow to come and mine goes unreturned: my reading that help here comes back falls.

Good mood raises helping (Carlson, Charlin and Miller 1988). Mood spreads through a group by contagion, and in one lab study groups exposed to pleasant contagion showed more cooperation and less conflict than those exposed to unpleasant contagion (Barsade 2002). That confidence in the venture carries such a mood is common sense, untested by these studies; if it does, help flows more freely in a group that expects to win. The decrement, each member guarding her own part when the venture looks beyond the group, is a proposal resting on common sense: people who doubt the shared outcome turn to securing their own. The step from the group's mood to her felt return is a proposal too: common sense, since a side that expects to win is a generous one. Where doubt about the venture rallies the group around a common threat (E:GrpProsp->Belonging), help may keep flowing; play the decrement weak or not at all then. Modest; forms a loop with E:Reciprocity->GrpProsp.

Backs to each other: Belonging to GrpProsp (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When the others draw me in as one of their own, I see us talk the work through, pass on what we know and pull the same way, and the venture looks within the reach of a side like ours: my confidence that the group, as it stands, can pull it off rises.

Decrement: When I am left at the edge, I see the work run in knots that do not talk it through or pass things on, and what I could bring left out of it, and the venture looks beyond the group as it stands: my confidence that the group can pull it off falls.

Cohesion is related to group performance, and all three of its components count, most for behaviour and efficiency and where work flows intensively between members (Beal et al. 2003). Belonging sits nearest the social component, interpersonal attraction, so the evidence for this card is indirect. Her Belonging reads the others' acceptance of her, not how close-knit the group is, so the step from her own inclusion to the group's cohesion is a proposal: a member left at the edge sees the group as split, and sees what she brings go unused. Where she is shut out by a group that plainly works well together, the decrement is weak or nil. Performance to cohesion is the stronger direction (Mullen and Copper 1994), carried by E:GrpProsp->Belonging, so set this card smaller than that one. It is distinct from E:Reciprocity->GrpProsp (help that comes back) and E:OutResp->GrpProsp (reliability).
