With E:Belonging->OutResp, E:GrpProsp->Reciprocity and E:OutResp->Levelling, it leaves E:OutResp->Reciprocity as the one empty ordered pair among the core deck E Pillars.

Rising tide: GrpProsp to OwnProsp (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When I feel those at the top can steer us through what we have taken on, I see what I came for riding on a venture in safe hands: a well-led side that wins has places, credit and shares to hand down, and my sense that staying will bring me what I came for rises.

Decrement: When I feel those at the top cannot steer us through what we have taken on, I see what I came for going down with a venture in the wrong hands: a badly led side has little to hand down and no name to lend me, and my sense that staying will bring me what I came for falls.

Deck H; the source is Team Confidence's hierarchical face. The mechanism is kept: where members' outcomes ride on the group's, the venture's prospects are part of each member's own. Reward interdependence acts on members' effort (Wageman 1995), and loafing falls when members value the group outcome and expect their effort to matter to it (Karau and Williams 1993). In a ranked group those prospects are read through the top, as Team Confidence's hierarchical face defines. Work on authority ranking (Fiske 1992), credit and blame given to leaders for group outcomes (Meindl, Ehrlich and Dukerich 1985), and leadership as a predictor of team performance and collective efficacy (Dirks 2000; Chen and Bliese 2002; Dirks and Ferrin 2002) points the same way but is pending a check and is not relied on here. How fairly the top will share out what the venture yields is Parity's or Reciprocity's ground, not this card's; the card reads only how much a well- or badly-led venture will have to hand out. No study here measures a member's forecast of her own yield, so the felt step is a proposal resting on common sense: nobody expects to get ahead under leaders who are running the side aground. Where she is at the top herself, her confidence in her own steering feeds her forecast through the venture; what her rung itself brings her is H:Status->OwnProsp. Set the card small or nil where her aims do not depend on the venture (a member there for the company, or paid by her own output alone). A run of results can inflate or sink the face beyond the leaders' real grip; the brake is Team Confidence evidence on the venture itself.

Nothing left for me: Levelling to OwnProsp (Reinforce, X)

provisional

Increment: When no member here can make me act or hold back through fear, none takes more than his due of the shares, the credit or the say and keeps it, and none hands things out to his own past me, what I came for is mine to work towards, and my sense that staying will bring it to me rises a little.

Decrement: When a member can make me comply through fear, takes more than his due of the shares, the credit or the say and keeps it, or hands out chances and shares to his own while I am passed over, I see what I came for going his way or hanging on his whim, and my sense that staying will bring me what I came for falls.

Distributive and procedural injustice each predict lower commitment and outcome satisfaction (Colquitt et al. 2001, organisational samples, injustice from those in authority). Abusive supervision is reported to go with lower commitment and higher intent to leave (Mackey et al. 2017); that finding is unconfirmed and carries no weight here until checked. Commitment and intent to leave are Engagement's ground; the card takes from these studies only the drop in what members expect to get, nearest to outcome satisfaction, so the support for Payoff is indirect. Extending them to any member who coerces, grabs or tilts the share-out to his own is a proposal, and the coercion-through-fear strand has no checked source and rests on common sense: where one member can take or block what the group would give, staying looks less likely to pay. Set the increment small, since freedom from a coercer opens no way by itself. Deck X: Parity is egalitarian, Payoff hierarchical. Distinct from Built-in Advantage (H:Status->OwnProsp), which runs through her own place in the order.

Following a lead I believe in: Engagement to GrpProsp (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When this group is part of who I am, I follow those at the top willingly, and what they steer us to reads as a sign of what they can do: my confidence that they can bring the venture off rises.

Decrement: When I am pulling out of this group, I follow half-heartedly, and each misstep from the top reads as the limit of what they can do: my confidence that they can bring the venture off falls.

Hierarchical-face twin of E:Engagement->Team Confidence, on the same grounds: investment carries enthusiasm or flatness that colours judgements built from ambiguous cues (Forgas 1995), and engagement feeds efficacy beliefs over time (Salanova, Llorens and Schaufeli 2011). Trust in leadership runs both ways with performance (Dirks 2000). The step from her own investment to confidence in those at the top is a proposal; keep it modest, and let Team Confidence evidence cards (a leader's visible failure) act as the brake.

Backers at my shoulder: Reciprocity to Status (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When the partners I help pay me back and the one above me covers me, a turn or share of mine that someone questions finds my partners moving to my side; the challenger gives way and I take it as of right: my felt rung in the order rises a little.

Decrement: When my partners take and do not return and the one above me no longer covers me, a challenge to my turn or share finds no one at my side; I give way, and the one who pressed me goes ahead of me next time too: my felt rung in the order falls.

The card reads Reciprocity's hierarchical face: return from particular partners, and favour and protection passed down from the one above in return for loyalty, as in patron and client ties (Scott 1972, to be checked). In primates grooming given is repaid in agonistic support (36 studies, 14 species, small effect: Schino 2007), and allied and kin support decides how macaque females acquire and hold rank (Chapais 1992). H:Belonging->Status hands partner support to Reciprocity but no card carried it; this one does. Support from particular partners and a patron, not the whole room's assent (Backed into my place). The effect per exchange is small, so the step is modest, and the increment is smaller than the decrement: backing firms up a contested turn more than it lifts her above her place.

Skill shared, drawn in: Prestige to Belonging (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When the others watch how I do things and bring me their problems, and I share what I know without lording it, they seek my company and keep a place for me wherever they gather: my sense that they want me among them rises.

Decrement: When no one watches or seeks me for anything I bring, I am the one who has to seek them out, and I read the quiet as being wanted less: my sense that they want me among them falls a little.

Prestige-based influence comes with being liked, dominance-based influence does not (Cheng et al. 2013, from a secondary summary; liking falls short of belonging). Learners defer to the models they learn from to gain access to what they know (Henrich and Gil-White 2001); that they then seek her company is a common-sense step from access. Under the E face, acceptance does not rest on output, so the rise runs through the liking and contact that come with being sought out, and through what she shares freely, which counts as pulling with the group; skill as output adds nothing by itself. Whether she carries it modestly is Repute's ground (E:Repute->Belonging; pack X:Prestige->Repute carries the boasting case). The decrement is small and lies in her reading, not in the group's acceptance, which still counts her one of their own: being sought less is easily felt as being wanted less, a common-sense step until a source on relational value (Leary and Baumeister 2000, unchecked) is read. A member who brings little but pulls as far as she is able stays one of their own in good standing, and the card must never edge her out on that ground alone.

Eyes on skill, not on the bully: Levelling to Prestige (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When no one here can make us do anything by force or fear, or hand things out to their own, the others' eyes go to whoever does the work best, and where that is me they watch, copy and come to me: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring rises.

Decrement: When a member makes us comply through fear or hands things out to his own, everyone's eyes track him instead; my way of doing things goes unwatched and what I could bring waits on his say: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring falls.

Dominant and prestigious members both draw more visual attention than others (Cheng et al. 2013, eye tracking). That a dominant's hold on attention leaves less for skilled members is a common-sense step, since attention in a small group is limited; the study did not test it. Cooperation in chimpanzees depends on tolerance between partners (Melis et al. 2006a), and chimpanzees recruit the more effective of two collaborators (Melis et al. 2006b). The step to her own felt deference is a proposal: keep it modest and scale it to what she brings.

Putting in, looked to: Engagement to Prestige (Reinforce, E)

provisional

Increment: When this group is part of who I am, I bring what I can to each venture and share it freely, and I read the others' glances and questions as turning to me for it: my sense that they look to me for what I bring rises.

Decrement: When I am pulling out of this group, I bring little and keep what I know to myself, and I read their turning to others as what I bring no longer counting: my sense that they look to me for what I bring falls.

Egalitarian-face twin of H:Engagement->Prestige, needed because every Pillar must have an Engagement card for the reflective beat. Members who contribute to the group earn status and influence (Willer 2009, laboratory public-goods studies), and in an egalitarian society leaders have more kin and exchange partners (von Rueden et al. 2014), so investment and visible contribution go together with being looked to. That investment also colours her reading of ambiguous glances and questions is a proposal resting on common sense; keep the step modest.

Steering on trial: GrpProsp to Status (Reinforce, H)

provisional

Increment: When I am among those at the top and feel sure we can steer the group through what it has taken on, the others wait for my call and leave the first turn to me as before: my felt rung in the order holds or rises a little.

Decrement: When I am among those at the top and feel we cannot steer it through, my calls come out hesitant, the first turn no longer falls to me without a word, someone questions it and I give ground: my felt rung in the order falls.

In a small-scale egalitarian society, leaders hold influence over collective action without formal office (von Rueden et al. 2014); the abstract ties that influence to strength, kin and exchange partners. Garfield, von Rueden and Hagen (2019) review political leadership from evolutionary anthropology, but the check did not read it, so it is not relied on here. Neither source, as checked, shows that a leader's standing tracks the group's prospects. That link, and the step from influence (which lies nearer Esteem) to settled precedence, are proposals resting on common sense: a member at the top who doubts the group can be steered through shows it in hesitant calls, others notice, and the first turn stops falling to her. Nil where she is not at the top. Keep the fall modest and slower than Esteem's.
